data: All APIs live under https://api.mapx.at/v1/ and need a free API token from account.mapx.at. Send it as Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN or ?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN; see Access and limits. mx_pk_ tokens (public) work from allowed websites and Android apps with GET/HEAD, mx_sk_ tokens (secret) from servers. The pages below are generated from the OpenAPI description and reflect the service as of the last docs build. Each page has a playground that calls the live API.
data.apis#APIs: Tiles Tileset list, TileJSON, XYZ tiles. Styles Styles, fonts, sprites, Static Tiles. Geocoding Forward, reverse and batch. Search Box Suggestions, retrieve, categories. Address Autofill and validation. Directions Routes, isochrone, matrix, matching, speed limits, corridor graph. Optimization Optimized trips and tour planning. Transit Journeys, stops, departures. Static Images Map images with overlays. Tilequery Vector tile features at a point. Elevation Heights and profiles. Weather Observations, forecast, warnings, tiles. Air quality Index, pollutants, Saharan dust. Climate Solar potential, normals, snow, drought. Traffic Incidents, gantry speed limits, tiles.
data.conventions#Conventions: Coordinates are lon,lat (WGS84), several separated by ;. See Coordinates. Errors are application/problem+json (RFC 9457) with a stable code, including 401/403 for token problems. See Errors and limits. Limits apply per IP address and zone, plus a per-minute limit per token; 429 carries Retry-After. See Access and limits. Caching: tiles, styles and TileJSON carry ETag; send If-None-Match to get 304. Versioning: the version is in the path. Fields do not change within a version, new ones are only added.
data.more-reference#More reference: Tilesets: data sheets of every tileset. Style specification, Terrain-RGB, Tile scheme. Errors and limits, Attribution. Status: health check of the API.

data:
Autofill completes a postal address while the user types. Validation checks an address against the official register.
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: search (10/s) · Guide: Search
data.address-autofill-retrieve-the-chosen-add:
GET /v1/autofill/retrieve/{id}
id from suggestions[].id (address-). FeatureCollection with one point feature; features[].id is the address id, properties carry the same fields as a suggestion (id, address_line1, street, housenumber, postcode, place, municipality, state, full_address, coordinates).
More session_token echoes the parameter (null without it). 404 for an unknown id.
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description id path string yes – Address id from suggest session_token query string – As in suggest Example
curlJavaScriptPython ID=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/suggest?q=Herrengasse%2013%20Wien&limit=1" | jq -r '.suggestions[0].id') curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/retrieve/$ID" | jq const headers = { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" }; const s = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/suggest?q=Herrengasse%2013%20Wien&limit=1", { headers })).json(); const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/retrieve/" + encodeURIComponent(s.suggestions[0].id), { headers }); const data = await res.json(); import requests h = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"} s = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/suggest?q=Herrengasse%2013%20Wien&limit=1", headers=h).json() res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/retrieve/" + s["suggestions"][0]["id"], headers=h) data = res.json() Example response
{ "type": "FeatureCollection", "session_token": null, "attribution": "mapx.at; Daten: BEV – Adressregister, Geonamen, Verwaltungsgrenzen, DKM (CC BY 4.0)", "features": [ { "type": "Feature", "id": "address-7065749", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [ 16.242382, 47.813929 ] }, "properties": { "id": "address-7065749", "address_line1": "Herrengasse 13", "street": "Herrengasse", "housenumber": "13", "postcode": "2700", "place": "Wiener Neustadt", "municipality": "Wiener Neustadt", "state": "Niederösterreich", "full_address": "Herrengasse 13, 2700 Wiener Neustadt", "coordinates": [ 16.242382, 47.813929 ] } } ] } Field Type Description session_token string,null The session_token parameter, echoed back (null without it). attribution string Data sources (CC BY 4.0), attribution required. features array One point feature; id is the address id address-, properties hold id, address_line1, street, housenumber, postcode, place, municipality, state, full_address and coordinates [lon, lat]. data.address-autofill-suggestions#Address Aut:
GET /v1/autofill/suggest
Official address register only (BEV). Completes street, house number, postcode and place; fields separated in suggestions[]. A complete place or postcode after the house number takes precedence as in geocode (Hauptplatz 12a Graz suggests addresses in Graz, nearest numbers first, if 12a does not exist there).
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description q query string yes – Partial input, e.g. Hauptpl 3 Mel session_token query string – Session id (1 to 64 characters), echoed back proximity query string – lon,lat, prefers near addresses limit query string 5 1 to 10, default 5 Example
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/suggest?q=Herrengasse%2013%20Wien&limit=3" | jq const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/suggest?q=Herrengasse%2013%20Wien&limit=3", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }); const data = await res.json(); import requests res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/autofill/suggest?q=Herrengasse%2013%20Wien&limit=3", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}) data = res.json() Example response

data.address-validation-free-text-or-structur:
GET /v1/address/validate
Checks an address against the official register. status: match | corrected | ambiguous | not_found. Returns the parsed input, the normalized address, confidence (0 to 1, 0 with not_found), deviations[] per field (kind: spelling | wrong | added | unknown), coordinates, id and address_code.
More Understands Str./Straße, abbreviations, umlauts and ß; a house number range (1-3) is not the number 13. A given place or postcode takes precedence: candidates elsewhere only count if none lies there. A different house number is never a correction: if the number does not exist in the street, status is not_found, deviations holds {"field": "housenumber", "kind": "unknown"} and candidates[] lists the nearest numbers of that street (up to 5), e.g. street=Rathausplatz&housenumber=999&postcode=3100. With ambiguous the fields address, coordinates, id and address_code are null and candidates[] (up to 5, each shaped like address) lists the possible addresses, e.g. q=Hauptplatz 3 (without place): {"status": "ambiguous", "address": null, "id": null, "candidates": [{"id": "address-5111737", "full_address": "Hauptplatz 3, 6511 Zams", ...}, {"id": "address-6067644", "full_address": "Hauptplatz 3, 9170 Ferlach", ...}]}. With match and corrected, candidates is empty.
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description q query string – Free text, e.g. Haubtplatz 1, 3390 Melk (or structured fields) street query string – Street housenumber query string – House number postcode query string – Postcode place query string – Place Example
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/address/validate?q=Haubtplatz%201,%203390%20Melk" | jq const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/address/validate?q=Haubtplatz%201,%203390%20Melk", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }); const data = await res.json(); import requests res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/address/validate?q=Haubtplatz%201,%203390%20Melk", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}) data = res.json() Example response
{ "status": "corrected", "confidence": 0.96, "input": { "street": "Haubtplatz", "housenumber": "1", "postcode": "3390", "place": "Melk" }, "attribution": "mapx.at; Daten: BEV – Adressregister, Geonamen, Verwaltungsgrenzen, DKM (CC BY 4.0)", "deviations": [ { "field": "street", "input": "Haubtplatz", "expected": "Hauptplatz", "kind": "spelling" } ], "address": { "id": "address-6444187", "address_line1": "Hauptplatz 1", "street": "Hauptplatz", "housenumber": "1", "postcode": "3390", "place": "Melk", "municipality": "Melk", "state": "Niederösterreich", "full_address": "Hauptplatz 1, 3390 Melk", "coordinates": [ 15.329515, 48.227317 ] }, "coordinates": [ 15.329515, 48.227317 ], "id": "address-6444187", "address_code": "6444187", "candidates": [] } Field Type Description status string match: found as given; corrected: found after corrections (see deviations); ambiguous: several addresses fit (see candidates); not_found: no address fits (if only the house number is unknown, candidates lists the nearest numbers of the street). confidence number 0 to 1; 0 with not_found. input object The input as understood: street, housenumber, postcode, place (parsed from q or taken from the structured fields). address object,null The normalized address (id, address_line1, street, housenumber, postcode, place, municipality, state, full_address, coordinates); null unless match or corrected. deviations array Per corrected field: field, input, expected, kind (spelling, wrong or added); with not_found for an unknown house number {field: housenumber, kind: unknown}. coordinates array,null [lon, lat] of the address, null unless match or corrected. id string,null Address id address- (as in Autofill and geocoding). address_code string,null Address code of the BEV address register. candidates array With ambiguous: up to 5 possible addresses; with not_found for an unknown house number: up to 5 nearest numbers of the street; each shaped like address; otherwise empty. attribution string Data sources (CC BY 4.0), attribution required. Errors (details: error catalog)
Status Meaning 400 A parameter is missing or invalid 401 Token missing or invalid (missing-token, invalid-token, token-expired) 403 Token not allowed here (origin-not-allowed, origin-missing, pk-not-allowed, app-not-allowed, token-blocked, ip-not-allowed) 429 Rate limit exceeded, wait Retry-After seconds 502 Upstream service unavailable

data:
Daily air quality index and hourly nitrogen dioxide, ozone, PM10 and PM2.5 near the surface plus the Saharan dust load for a point, from the GeoSphere chemical weather model (3 km). The index follows the EEA European Air Quality Index (1 good to 6 extremely poor; SO2 is not provided by the model). Map layers: the weather tiles aqi, no2, o3, pm10, pm25 and dust (see Weather API). Source: GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0.
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: search (10/s) · Guide: Maps
data.air-quality-index-and-pollutants-for-a-p:
GET /v1/air-quality/{coordinate}
GeoSphere chemical weather model (3 km) bilinear to the point: daily index aqi (3 days) and hourly NO2, O3, PM10, PM2.5 near the surface in ug/m3 with an hourly index (worst level by the EEA European Air Quality Index limits; SO2 is not provided by the model) plus the Saharan dust load (mg/m2, 0.2 degree grid).
More Austria and surroundings. Data source: GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0 (attribution required).
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description coordinate path string yes – lon,lat, e.g. 16.37,48.21 hours query integer 24 1 to 72, default 24; the daily run (00 UTC) reaches 48 h, fewer hours are marked with truncated: true Example
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/air-quality/16.3725,48.2085?hours=6" | jq const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/air-quality/16.3725,48.2085?hours=6", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }); const data = await res.json(); import requests res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/air-quality/16.3725,48.2085?hours=6", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}) data = res.json() Example response

data:
Climate of a point: yearly solar radiation and sunshine hours, temperature and precipitation normals with trend, hot and frost days, snow days per winter and the drought index. Source: GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0.
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: search (10/s) · Guide: Maps
data.climate-at-a-point-solar-potential-norma:
GET /v1/climate/{coordinate}
Climate of one point from open data of GeoSphere Austria: solar potential (yearly global radiation in kWh/m2 and modelled sunshine hours, mean of the last 3 complete years, 100 m), temperature and precipitation (normal 1991-2020, last 10 years, trend, monthly normals, 1 km), hot/summer/frost/ice days and tropical nights per year, snow days per winter and the current snow depth, and the drought index SPEI (90 and 365 days, latest value with class).
More Each section has source (dataset, cell, last day of data) and retrieved_at. Values are derived per grid cell and cached; the first request for a new cell fetches them from the source and can take 10 to 20 seconds (sections limits the work), later requests come from the cache. Outside Austria 404 outside-coverage; unreadable coordinates 400 invalid-coordinates; 503 while the source is unavailable or rate limited. Data source: GeoSphere Austria (APOLIS, SPARTACUS, SNOWGRID-CL, WINFORE), CC BY 4.0 (attribution required).
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description coordinate path string yes – lon,lat or lon,lat.json sections query string all Comma-separated sections to return (default: all) Example
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/climate/15.3294,48.2272?sections=solar,snow" | jq const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/climate/15.3294,48.2272?sections=solar,snow", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }); const data = await res.json(); import requests res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/climate/15.3294,48.2272?sections=solar,snow", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}) data = res.json() Example response

data:
Routing on the Austrian road graph (GIP.at). Profiles: driving, driving-traffic, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb, walking.
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: route (5/s), heavy (30/min) · Guide: Navigation
data.corridor-graph-for-offline-rerouting#Cor:
GET /v1/corridor-graph
Compact binary subgraph of the road network around a route, for recomputing a route without network (for example in a dead zone after a wrong turn). polyline is the route as polyline6 (e.g. routes[].geometry with geometries=polyline6), buffer the radius around it in meters (default 3000, at most 5000).
Needs a secret token (mx_sk_); public tokens get 403 pk-not-allowed, so the playground cannot run it.
More The response body is a gzip stream (application/vnd.mapx.corridor-graph+gzip, no Content-Encoding) of a MXCG v1 file: a version header and the graph id of the server graph, nodes (microdegrees), directed arcs with travel time and weight in ms (the same values the router uses, so offline costs equal server costs), simplified link geometry, road name and reference, road class (FRC/FOW), maximum speed with a statutory flag, link flags (roundabout, ramp, toll, urban, motorway) and the turn restrictions between the arcs including derived U-turn bans. Arcs that cannot be driven are left out. Typically 1 to 3 MB per 100 km of route (compressed). Source: GIP.at (CC BY 4.0).
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description polyline query string yes – Route as polyline6 (at most 20,000 points) profile query string – driving (default), cycling or walking buffer query string 3000 Meters around the route, 100 to 5000, default 3000 Example
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/corridor-graph?polyline=_wp~zAofsf%5C_nDouS_pR_af@&buffer=1000" -o result.bin const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/corridor-graph?polyline=_wp~zAofsf%5C_nDouS_pR_af@&buffer=1000", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }); const blob = await res.blob(); import requests res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/corridor-graph?polyline=_wp~zAofsf%5C_nDouS_pR_af@&buffer=1000", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}) open("result.bin", "wb").write(res.content) Example response: application/vnd.mapx.corridor-graph+gzip · Corridor graph (gzip of MXCG v1)
Errors (details: error catalog)
Status Meaning 400 A parameter is missing or invalid 401 Token missing or invalid (missing-token, invalid-token, token-expired) 403 Token not allowed here (origin-not-allowed, origin-missing, pk-not-allowed, app-not-allowed, token-blocked, ip-not-allowed) 404 Not found (name, path or position) 429 Rate limit exceeded, wait Retry-After seconds 502 Upstream service unavailable
data.directions-with-query-parameters#Directi:
GET /v1/directions
Same response as /v1/directions/{profile}/{coordinates} (preferred); all query parameters of the path form apply.
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description profile query string driving Default driving coordinates query string yes – lon,lat;lon,lat;… steps query string – true for turn-by-turn steps (with maneuvers and intersections) geometries query string – geojson (default) | polyline | polyline6 overview query string – simplified (default, simplified route geometry), full (every vertex) or false (no geometry) language query string – de (default) or en for instructions and announcements; other values 400 alternatives query string – true (up to 2), false or 0 to 3; only with exactly 2 coordinates. Alternatives are built via laterally offset waypoints and appear as additional routes[] annotations query string – duration, distance, speed, maxspeed, elevation, weather_warnings (comma-separated; weather_warnings adds routes[].weather_warnings, the official warnings whose area the route crosses, without geometry): legs[].annotation per geometry segment; speed in m/s, maxspeed [{speed, unit: km/h, legal} | {unknown: true}] (driving only; legal is true for a statutory limit and false for a modeled speed such as 53 or 84 that must not be shown as a limit), elevation = mean segment height in m radiuses query string – Search radius per coordinate in meters, semicolon-separated, or unlimited (20 km); each coordinate snaps within its own radius, otherwise 404 approaches query string – unrestricted or curb per coordinate (validated, not yet used by the router) bearings query string – degrees,tolerance per coordinate (validated, not yet used by the router) incidents query string true for driving-traffic true/false: traffic incidents along the leg as legs[].incidents; default true for driving-traffic, otherwise false; cars only exclude query string – motorway, toll and/or ferry, comma-separated: motorway avoids motorways (category A; driving, driving-traffic, driving-truck); toll avoids all toll roads: vignette-required ASFINAG motorways and expressways (categories A and S) and special-toll sections (A9 Gleinalm/Bosruck, A10 Tauern/Katschberg, A11 Karawanken, A13 Brenner, S16 Arlberg; same profiles). data.isochrones#Isochrones:
GET /v1/isochrone/{profile}/{coordinate}
Reachable areas, largest first; properties.contour/color/opacity. Zone heavy. Profile transit computes walking plus public transport (GTFS timetable, RAPTOR): walk to stops, ride from depart_at, walk on from every stop reached; only contours_minutes (default 5,10,15, at most 120 min), the timetable’s validity period applies (otherwise 422), metadata carries depart_at, transit_stops and attribution.
More access=foot|bike|car (default foot) chooses how the first stop is reached: bike = Bike & Ride (bike to any stop, +2 min for locking), car = Park & Ride (drive, at most 25 min, to stops with rail/metro/tram service, +3 min for parking, and to official GIP P+R sites, +2 min and a walk to the stop); the fastest combination wins, exit is always on foot. park=official restricts parking to official P+R/B+R sites. metadata then adds access, park, access_stops_improved and access_sites (top sites entries: source site|stop, kind, name, lon, lat, arrive_min, ready_min, stops_won). Bike carriage on trains is not in the timetable data, so there is no egress=bike. The other profiles reject depart_at, access and park (400).

data.map-matching#Map matching:
GET /v1/matching/{profile}/{coordinates}
2 to 100 GPS points snapped to the road network. Without timestamps a single point far off the trace (out and straight back, both legs over 300 m and together more than 3 times the direct distance) counts as an outlier: its tracepoint is null and the matching continues.
More Consecutive points more than 5 km (or, with timestamps, 300 s) apart split the trace into several matchings. If no part can be matched the response is 422 (No match). Longer traces: POST https://routing.mapx.at/match with a secret token (mx_sk_…; public tokens allow GET only) and a JSON body {"coordinates": [[lon, lat], ...], "timestamps": [...], "radius": 25} (at most 512 KB); it answers in its own form, not the Mapbox form: a GeoJSON FeatureCollection with one LineString per matched segment plus tracepoints (snapped point and confidence per input point, null if unmatched).

data.routing#Routing:
GET /v1/directions/{profile}/{coordinates}
Trucks (driving-truck, over 3.5 t): vehicle size via weight, height, width, length, truck_type; roads are blocked per vehicle (weight-class, semi and trailer bans, height/width/weight/length limits). Truck speeds: at most 80 km/h on motorways, 70 on rural roads, 50 in built-up areas.
More District-wide bans (free-text ordinances) are not routed; affected roads appear as steps[].notices[] (type: truck_restriction). Responses add routes[].truck (the vehicle used) and routes[].toll.truck_go_km (kilometers subject to the GO toll; per step truck_go_m). 2 to 25 coordinates; legs are computed individually. Car routes (driving) contain routes[].toll (vignette and special-toll data), toll_road, toll_road_m and steps[].intersections[].classes; toll source ASFINAG, CC BY 4.0. From the GIP, steps additionally carry ref, destinations, milestone, maxspeed, ascent_m, descent_m and (cycling/walking) grade_pct, for cycling and cycling-mtb also bike_infrastructure (cycleway, lane, shared, none) and surface (paved, cobblestone, unpaved, offroad, unknown); routes[].summary has ascent, descent, max grade and elevation range. The default overview=simplified returns a simplified geometry, steps=true adds step geometry and intersections. Closures: driving, driving-traffic and driving-truck avoid the active full closures from the traffic reports (EVIS/ASFINAG, closed: true in /v1/traffic/incidents). Binding closures (EVIS compliance option mandatory, traffic regulations) are never driven; full closures without that flag, such as winter closures of passes, are driven only as a last resort, when start or destination lies on or behind them. routes[].closures_avoided lists the closures the route without closures would have used (binding tells the two apart), routes[].closures_unavoidable those the route still runs through. Time-conditional regulations (weekdays or hours only in the text) are only discouraged, and only by driving-traffic. Cycling and walking ignore the closures (the reports concern motor traffic). driving-traffic additionally slows motorway sections where ASFINAG variable message signs show a limit below free-flow speed (see /v1/traffic/sign-limits); there is no area-wide live traffic state. Navigation: steps=true with voice_instructions=true and/or banner_instructions=true adds Mapbox-style voice and banner instructions (all road profiles, texts in language). Speed limits: maxspeed (step and annotation) is {speed, unit, legal}; legal: true marks a statutory limit (5, 10, 20 … 130 km/h), legal: false a modeled GIP speed (e.g. 53, 84) that is not a limit; {unknown: true} without a value (backward compatible: speed and unit are unchanged). For limits along a corridor see /v1/speedlimits.

data.elevation-profile-along-a-line#Elevation:
GET /v1/elevation/profile
One GeoJSON line; properties: distances, elevations, ascent_m, descent_m, ascent_threshold_m, min_m, max_m. Ascent and descent are counted with hysteresis: a rise or fall counts only once the elevation has moved at least ascent_threshold_m (3 m) from the last turning point, so the totals hardly depend on samples and terrain noise is not summed up (flat Marchfeld, 9.6 km: 0 m instead of 46 m unfiltered; Grossglockner High Alpine Road up from Heiligenblut: about 1150 m).
More With model=dsm buildings and vegetation count as terrain, so ascent is higher. The line has z coordinates when every sample has an elevation; otherwise all positions are 2D and the gaps are null in elevations. For a route geometry use the POST form.

Same response as GET. Body: a GeoJSON LineString, a Feature with a LineString (e.g. routes[0].geometry from /v1/directions?geometries=geojson&overview=full) or {"coordinates": [[lon, lat], ...]}, 2 to 20000 vertices; samples and model in the body or as query parameters.
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description samples query integer (2–1024) 100 2 to 1024, default 100 model query dtm | dsm dtm dtm (default) or dsm Request body (JSON)
{ "type": "LineString", "coordinates": [ [ 12.8418, 47.0378 ], [ 12.7865, 47.0739 ], [ 12.7303, 47.0792 ] ] } Example

data.elevations-bilinear-from-z16-terrain-rgb:
GET /v1/elevation
Either points (up to 512 points) or path (polyline on the sphere, split evenly by length into samples points). Outside the area elevation is null. The gateway limits the request URL to about 8 KB (longer URLs get 414 as problem+json), so in practice a GET carries about 400 points with 6 decimals, fewer with more digits.
More Split larger point sets into several requests; for points along a line send only the vertices as path and let samples (up to 1024) do the sampling, or send the line to POST /v1/elevation/profile (up to 20000 vertices).
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description points query string – lon,lat;lon,lat;… (at most 512; the URL limit of about 8 KB usually allows fewer) path query string – lon,lat;lon,lat;… (2 to 512 vertices) samples query integer (2–1024) 100 With path only model query dtm | dsm dtm dtm (terrain) or dsm (surface) Example
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation?points=12.694,47.074;15.3294,48.2272&model=dtm" | jq const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation?points=12.694,47.074;15.3294,48.2272&model=dtm", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }); const data = await res.json(); import requests res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation?points=12.694,47.074;15.3294,48.2272&model=dtm", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}) data = res.json() Example response
{ "type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [ { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [ 16.3725, 48.2083 ] }, "properties": { "elevation": 171.3, "resolution_m": 1, "model": "dtm", "reference_date": "2025-09-15" } } ] } Errors (details: error catalog)

data:
Every error is an application/problem+json document (RFC 9457). The type is a URI into this page: https://docs.mapx.at/api/errors/#. Branch on code (or type) and status, never on the text.
{ "type": "https://docs.mapx.at/api/errors/#invalid-parameter", "title": "Invalid parameter", "status": 400, "detail": "types: unknown value 'foo' (allowed: address, street, locality, place, district, region, postcode, poi, road_ref)", "code": "invalid-parameter", "param": "types", "allowed": ["address", "street", "locality", "place", "district", "region", "postcode", "poi", "road_ref"] }
data.app-not-allowed#app-not-allowed:
403 · App not allowed
A public token bound to an Android app was used with a package name or signing certificate that does not match.
What to do: Send the headers X-Mapx-Android-Package and X-Mapx-Android-Cert of the registered app, or fix the binding in your account.
data.attribution#Attribution: JSON responses carrying data have a top-level attribution field (plain text, no HTML) naming the source to credit when displaying or passing on the data. It always starts with mapx.at; , e.g. mapx.at; Datenquelle: GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0 (…) for weather or mapx.at; Datenquelle: GIP.at … for routing, matrix and isochrone. Exceptions: the lists /v1/styles, /v1/fonts, /v1/sprites (arrays); styles credit their sources in sources, mapx.at as the first source mapx. See Attribution.
data.authentication-errors#Authentication err:
Every request needs a token (Access and limits). Authentication errors answer 401 or 403 as application/problem+json; the code is also in the response header X-Mapx-Reason (readable from browser scripts). Requests without a token get 401 missing-token.
These answers come from the token check in the gateway in front of the API. They have the same shape as all other errors: a title and detail per reason (for example Access token required for missing-token, Invalid access token for invalid-token), always English. Branch on code or X-Mapx-Reason.
{"type": "https://docs.mapx.at/api/errors/#missing-token", "title": "Access token required", "status": 401, "detail": "Send the token as 'Authorization: Bearer ' or '?access_token='.", "code": "missing-token"} The other errors the gateway produces itself (404 unknown-path, 405, 413, 414, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504) are application/problem+json too, with type, title, detail and code. The gateway checks the method before the token: a method that is not allowed gives 405 even when the token is missing.
# with an invalid or unknown token (here the placeholder itself) the answer is 401 invalid-token curl -si -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Melk" | head -12
data.bad-request#bad-request:
400 · Bad request
The request is invalid in a way no more specific code covers.
What to do: Read detail and fix the request.
data.cache-unavailable#cache-unavailable:
503 · Authorization backend unavailable
The store behind the token check is briefly unreachable and the token is not in the local cache. The request is refused to stay on the safe side.
What to do: Retry after a few seconds.
data.caching#Caching: Header Value Cache-Control private for every response to a request with a token (browser cache only, no shared caches), with max-age=3600 (tiles.mapx.at, TileJSON, elevation), max-age=86400 (tiles via api.mapx.at), max-age=60 (Search Box suggestions, traffic), max-age=30 (departures), max-age=300 (geocoding, reverse, autofill suggestions, address validation via GET, tileset list), max-age=0 (routing, matrix, isochrone, POST requests); /health no-store ETag on every GET response; with If-None-Match → 304 without body. Tiles, styles, TileJSON and OpenAPI: version of the file (plus Last-Modified, If-Modified-Since), all others: hash of the content Server-Timing router, search, render, total in milliseconds RateLimit-Policy zone and limit of the endpoint (set by the gateway) PMTiles files carry the release date in their name and never change; they may be cached indefinitely.

data.forbidden#forbidden:
403 · Forbidden
Access is refused without a more specific reason, for example a path that is blocked at the gateway.
What to do: Compare path and host with the OpenAPI description.
data.internal-error#internal-error:
500 · Internal error
An unexpected error occurred on the server or in the gateway.
What to do: Retry once; if it persists, report the request.
data.invalid-body#invalid-body:
400 · Invalid request body
The body of a POST request is not valid JSON or not in the expected shape.
What to do: Check the JSON against the schema in the OpenAPI description.
data.invalid-coordinates#invalid-coordinates:
400 · Invalid coordinates
A coordinate (path segment or parameter) cannot be parsed or is outside the valid range. Unparsable path coordinates answer 400, not 404.
What to do: Send lon,lat in WGS84 degrees (longitude -180 to 180, latitude -90 to 90).
data.invalid-parameter#invalid-parameter:
400 · Invalid parameter
A parameter has a value that is malformed, out of range or not one of the accepted values. param names it; for enumerations allowed lists the accepted values.
What to do: Use a value from allowed or inside the range stated in detail.
data.invalid-path#invalid-path:
403 · Invalid request path
The request path has an invalid percent-encoding, a NUL byte or leaves the root with ...
What to do: Send a normal path as listed in the OpenAPI description.
data.invalid-token#invalid-token:
401 · Invalid access token
The token is malformed or unknown (also after it was deleted or rotated).
What to do: Copy the token again from your account, check for a stray space or line break, and use the current token. Tokens start with mx_pk_, mx_sk_ or (MCP server only) mx_mcp_.
data.ip-not-allowed#ip-not-allowed:
403 · IP not allowed
The secret token is restricted to IP ranges and the request comes from another address.
What to do: Add the address (CIDR) to the token or send from an allowed host.
data.language#Language: detail is always English and names the exact limit or value (for example limit: 1 to 10). With Accept-Language: de the title is German, detail stays the same, so nothing gets lost; authentication errors and the other gateway errors (405, 413, 414, 429, 5xx) are always English (unknown-path is available in German). type, code, param and allowed never depend on the language. Responses carry Content-Language and Vary: Accept-Language.
data.mcp-token-only#mcp-token-only:
403 · MCP token only valid at the MCP server
A token of type AI assistant (mx_mcp_) was used for a direct API call. It only works at the MCP server.
What to do: Use a secret token (mx_sk_) for direct API calls.
data.mcp-token-required#mcp-token-required:
403 · MCP token required
The MCP server https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp only accepts tokens of type AI assistant (mx_mcp_); a public or secret token was sent.
What to do: Create a token of type AI assistant (MCP) at account.mapx.at.
data.method-not-allowed#method-not-allowed:
405 · Method not allowed
Only GET (and HEAD) is allowed, POST only for batch geocoding, optimization, address validation and traffic incidents. The Allow header lists the allowed methods (e.g. POST /v1/geocode → 405, Allow: GET, HEAD). The gateway checks the method before the token, so 405 also comes when the token is missing as well.
What to do: Use a method from Allow.
data.missing-parameter#missing-parameter:
400 · Missing parameter
A required parameter is missing. param names it.
What to do: Add the parameter named in param.
data.missing-token#missing-token:
401 · Access token required
The request carries no token.
What to do: Create a token at account.mapx.at and send it as Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN or ?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN. See Access and limits.
data.not-found#not-found:
404 · Not found
The addressed resource (a tile, a sprite, …) does not exist.
What to do: Check the path. Tiles inside the zoom range without data answer 204, not this error.
data.origin-missing#origin-missing:
403 · Origin missing
A public token restricted to websites was used without Origin and without Referer, so the site cannot be checked.
What to do: Call from a browser page, or use a secret token on a server.
data.origin-not-allowed#origin-not-allowed:
403 · Origin not allowed
A public token (mx_pk_) was used from a website whose Origin (or Referer host) is not in the allowed origins of the token.
What to do: Add the origin to the token (for development also localhost), or call the API from your server with a secret token.
data.outside-coverage#outside-coverage:
404 · Outside coverage
The point lies outside the area for which the data exist (weather, nowcast, air quality and climate cover Austria and its surroundings). detail names the data and adds “(lon and lat swapped?)” when the swapped coordinates would be inside.
What to do: Send a point in Austria as lon,lat (longitude about 9.5 to 17.2, latitude about 46.4 to 49.0).
data.payload-too-large#payload-too-large:
413 · Payload too large
The request body is larger than the endpoint accepts: batch geocoding 512 KB, optimization 256 KB, traffic incidents 64 KB, all other POST endpoints (such as address validation) 16 KB; the MCP server 256 KB.
What to do: Split or shrink the request.
data.pk-not-allowed#pk-not-allowed:
403 · Public token not allowed here
A public token only allows read access (GET, HEAD) to the public products. Batch geocoding (POST /v1/geocode/batch), optimization (POST /v1/optimization), address validation via POST /v1/address/validate, traffic incidents via POST /v1/traffic/incidents and GET /v1/corridor-graph need a secret token.
What to do: Use a secret token (mx_sk_) from a server for this request.
data.quota-exceeded#quota-exceeded:
429 · Quota exceeded
The daily or monthly limit of the account is used up (all tokens of the account together, days and months in UTC). Currently both limits are unlimited, see access and limits.
What to do: Retry-After gives the seconds until the next day or month (UTC); retrying earlier does not help. Your account shows the usage under Usage.
data.range-required#range-required:
403 · Range required
tiles.mapx.at serves PMTiles files only in pieces: a GET on a .pmtiles file needs exactly one closed Range header (bytes=-). Requests without Range, with an open (bytes=100-), suffix (bytes=-500) or multiple range are refused. MapLibre with pmtiles.js and the mapx styles send valid ranges on their own. The gateway checks this before the token, like the method.
What to do: Load maps through the style, TileJSON or {z}/{x}/{y} tiles. Whole files are not offered for download.
data.rate-limited#rate-limited:
429 · Rate limit exceeded
Too many requests. 429 has two causes: the limit per IP address and zone (endpoint group) or the per-minute limit of the token. Both answer with title Rate limit exceeded, a detail and Retry-After. See rate limits.
Expensive groups also have an overall limit for all clients together; reaching it answers the same way.
What to do: Wait Retry-After seconds, then retry with growing back-off. The RateLimit-Policy header of every response (set by the gateway from its zone table) shows the zone.
data.rate-limits#Rate limits: Limits per IP address and zone and the per-minute limit per token are listed under Access and limits. Retry on 429 and 503 with growing delay and honor Retry-After; do not retry 400, 401, 403, 404 and 422 unchanged.
data.service-busy#service-busy:
503 · Service busy
The server is at its concurrency limit.
What to do: Wait Retry-After seconds and retry.
data.service-unavailable#service-unavailable:
503 · Service unavailable
The data or service is temporarily unavailable (e.g. weather data not loaded yet, a style being rebuilt).
What to do: Retry later.
data.tile-out-of-range#tile-out-of-range:
404 · Tile out of range
The tile is outside the zoom or tile range of the tileset or style.
What to do: Stay within minzoom/maxzoom and bounds of the TileJSON.
data.token-blocked#token-blocked:
403 · Access token blocked
The token was blocked in your account.
What to do: Unblock it in your account or use another token.
data.token-expired#token-expired:
401 · Access token expired
The token is past its expiry date.
What to do: Create or rotate a token in your account.
data.unknown-font#unknown-font:
404 · Unknown font
The font name is not known.
What to do: List fonts with /v1/fonts.
data.unknown-id#unknown-id:
404 · Unknown id
A suggestion, address or place id is not known (or expired after a data update).
What to do: Search again and use the id from the fresh response.
data.unknown-layer#unknown-layer:
404 · Unknown layer
A weather or air-quality layer (path of /v1/weather/tiles/…, /v1/air-quality/tiles/…) is not known.
What to do: Use one of temperature, precipitation, wind, humidity, cloud, pressure, aqi, no2, o3, pm10, pm25, dust, snowlimit, sunshine, radiation, cape, snowfall, rr_nowcast, pt_nowcast (list: /v1/weather/tiles/.json).
data.unknown-parameter#unknown-parameter:
400 · Unknown parameter
The endpoint does not know a query parameter or a field of the JSON body (often a typo, e.g. limt instead of limit). param names it, detail lists the known parameters of the endpoint. access_token is accepted everywhere.
What to do: Fix the name or drop the parameter; the parameters of each endpoint are in the OpenAPI description.
data.unknown-path#unknown-path:
404 · Unknown path
The path does not exist.
What to do: Check the path against the OpenAPI description. An unknown routing profile such as the former driving-ev answers 400 invalid-parameter.
data.unknown-style#unknown-style:
404 · Unknown style
The style id is not known.
What to do: List styles with /v1/styles.
data.unknown-tileset#unknown-tileset:
404 · Unknown tileset
The tileset name is not known.
What to do: List tilesets with /v1/tiles.
data.unprocessable#unprocessable:
422 · Unprocessable request
The request is well-formed but cannot be answered, e.g. no route between the points or a date outside the timetable period.
What to do: Change the points or the time; read detail.
data.upstream-error#upstream-error:
502 · Upstream error
A backing service (search, router) did not answer or answered with an error.
What to do: Retry after a few seconds.
data.upstream-timeout#upstream-timeout:
504 · Upstream timeout
The service behind the gateway did not answer in time.
What to do: Retry after a few seconds; split large requests.
See also: Access and limits for rate limits and caching.
data.uri-too-long#uri-too-long:
414 · URI too long
The request URL is longer than about 8 KB, for example very many points on /v1/elevation.
What to do: Send fewer values per request or, where the endpoint offers it, use POST with a JSON body.

/api/errors/.title: Errors, status codes and rate limits

data:
Turns an address or place name into coordinates and coordinates into the nearest address.
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: search (10/s), heavy (30/min) · Guide: Search
data.batch-geocoding-up-to-1000-requests#Batc:
POST /v1/geocode/batch
JSON array; each item has q or structured street/housenumber/postcode/place, optional types (string or list), limit (1 to 10), proximity [lon,lat], bbox. Response: array in input order with one FeatureCollection per item (same fields as geocode, including the place precedence and coordinates as q); an invalid item does not fail the batch but is answered at its position with a problem object (RFC 9457: type, title, status 400, detail, code, param).
Needs a secret token (mx_sk_); public tokens get 403 pk-not-allowed, so the playground cannot run it.
More A malformed body (no array, empty, more than 1000 items) still gives 400 for the whole call. proximity only orders equally good matches here (no separate nearby search as in geocode). Items are searched in chunks, at most 4 in parallel; the whole batch counts as one request in the rate limit. At most 512 KB.
Request body (JSON)
[ { "q": "Herrengasse 13 Wien", "types": "address", "limit": 1 }, { "street": "Hauptplatz", "housenumber": "3", "postcode": "3390" } ] Example
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -X POST "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode/batch" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '[{"q":"Herrengasse 13 Wien","types":"address","limit":1},{"street":"Hauptplatz","housenumber":"3","postcode":"3390"}]' | jq const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode/batch", { method: "POST", headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN", "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify([ { "q": "Herrengasse 13 Wien", "types": "address", "limit": 1 }, { "street": "Hauptplatz", "housenumber": "3", "postcode": "3390" } ]), }); const data = await res.json(); import requests res = requests.post("https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode/batch", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}, json=[ { "q": "Herrengasse 13 Wien", "types": "address", "limit": 1 }, { "street": "Hauptplatz", "housenumber": "3", "postcode": "3390" } ]) data = res.json() Example response (shortened: lists show only their first entries)

data.forward-geocoding#Forward geocoding:
GET /v1/geocode
Search over the official address register, streets, places, municipalities, districts, postcodes and points of interest. Road kilometers: B83 km 329,7, A1 km 41 or L190 km 3.5 (class A, S, B or L, number, the word km) return the point on the road at that kilometer as place_type road_ref with properties.road_ref (ref, km); the index holds a point every 0.1 km on motorways, expressways and federal roads and every 0.5 km on state roads (GIP.at), the nearest one is returned, the same state road number in several states gives several hits.
More Addresses: when the input names a place or postcode after the house number (Hauptplatz 12a Graz, Rathausplatz 1, 3100), hits in that place come first; if the number does not exist there, the base number (12 for 12a), the street in that place and the nearest numbers follow, never the same number in another place first. House number ranges (1-3, 15 - 16) stay ranges. Common abbreviations are expanded (Hptpl., Str., Hauptstr., Rathauspl., Pl., G., Bhf). Coordinates as search text (16.37,48.21 or 48.21, 16.37, both with a decimal point; order detected from Austria’s range) answer like /v1/reverse with query [lon, lat]. Response: FeatureCollection with place_type, place_name, center, geometry, bbox; relevance is the match score of the search (0 to 1, lower for a fallback to the base number, street or a neighboring number); for addresses and streets properties.address holds the separate fields (street, housenumber, postcode, place, locality, municipality, district, state) and properties.accuracy is rooftop (point on the building), parcel (point on the plot) or street. Waters (lakes, rivers, streams from the BEV geographical names) are place hits with properties.class see, fluss, bach or gewaesser. query lists the search words without punctuation. Always pass types for cheap queries.
Parameters

2 to 25 coordinates. Exact up to 12 points, above that nearest neighbour with 2-opt and Or-opt over the duration matrix. Response like Directions: trips[] with one route, waypoints[] in input order with waypoint_index (position in the trip) and trips_index.

data:
Incident reports (accidents, roadworks, closures), speed limits shown on motorway gantries and a vector layer for maps.
Base URL: https://api.mapx.at · Rate-limit zone: search (10/s), static (5/s) · Guide: Traffic
data.incident-reports-and-traffic-regulations:
GET /v1/traffic/incidents
Active reports (active=false: also ended and future), filterable by area, road (road, road_class), route, type and time window. Sorted by importance (closures and binding reports first, then motorways, expressways, federal and state roads, then start), paged with limit and cursor (total, next as relative URL or null on the last page; next_cursor and next_offset only when there is a further page).
More Roadworks on motorways and expressways carry lane details from ASFINAG (lanes). mandatory=true: binding (router: closure), show the text unchanged. Geometry along GIP edges. Fields: type (accident, congestion, construction, lane_restriction, road_closure, road_hazard, miscellaneous) and impact (critical: closed for cars; major: binding, lane restriction or accident; minor: other unplanned; low: other planned) are derived by mapx. kind is the category of the source in German (e.g. Straßensperre, Bauarbeiten, Belagsarbeiten, Instandhaltung), management its English counterpart or the DATEX II measure. closed is true only when the road is closed for cars; a road_closure with closed: false is closed for other modes only (see transport_modes, e.g. pedestrians, cycles) or traffic is led through on the opposite carriageway. road is the road number (A1, S33, B17, L347; derived from the road graph if the source has none, null for municipal streets), road_section the source id of a ramp or branch (A13.33.4). road_name, direction (text), regions (federal states) and creator come from EVIS. Times are UTC. Texts are plain text; angle brackets from the source are removed. Data source: ASFINAG / EVIS.AT (CC BY 4.0), road network GIP.at (CC BY 4.0); attribution required.
Parameters
Name In Type Required Default Description bbox query string – west,south,east,north; optional planned query string – true: planned only, false: unplanned only road query string – Road number, normalized: A1, A 1 and A01 are the same; also S1, B99, L347. Includes ramps and junction branches of the road (road_section A13.33.4 belongs to A13) road_class query string – Comma-separated: motorway (A), expressway (S), federal (B), state (L) active query string true true: only reports active now (default true; with from or to the default is false); false: also ended and future reports type query string – Comma-separated: accident, congestion, construction, lane_restriction, road_closure, road_hazard, miscellaneous from query string – Window start: date YYYY-MM-DD (00:00 UTC) or RFC 3339 date-time with Z or offset (2026-12-01T10:00:00+01:00); incidents still valid afterwards to query string – Window end, same format: incidents starting before. Must not be before from (400) route query string – Route corridor: encoded polyline (like geometries=polyline6 or polyline) or GeoJSON LineString; result sorted by position on the route route_precision query string – 6 (default) or 5 buffer query string 25 Corridor half-width in meters, 1 to 1000, default 25 sort query string – importance: closures and binding reports first, then road class A, S, B, L, then start (used when sort is not given); route: position on the route (used when sort is not given and route is set) limit query string 500 At most this many features, 0 to 1000, default 500 cursor query string – Page marker: next_cursor of the previous response offset query string – Skip features (alternative to cursor) Example

data.public-transit-walking-plus-transit-gtfs:
GET /v1/directions/transit/{coordinates}
Exactly origin and destination. Connections with walks on the GIP.at network and rides (line, stops, times, platform at from, to and stops[] where known, otherwise null). Time via depart_at (default now) or arrive_by, ISO 8601 in Vienna local time; invalid dates or times such as T25:00 or 2026-02-31 answer 400.
More line.name is the public line name as in /v1/departures (U3, S50, R52, long-distance trains by train number such as RJ 754), trip_short_name the train number. Changing at the same station takes at least 2 minutes, after a walk at least 1 minute remains before the departure. At most routes connections, sorted by arrival (depart_at) or by departure, latest first (arrive_by); connections that are no better than another (not earlier, not faster, not fewer rides) and coupled trains with identical times appear once. A direct walk comes first when it is not slower than the best ride. timetable gives the loaded timetable period (valid_from, valid_to); outside it, and when no stop is within reach or no connection is found, 422. Timetable data: ÖBB-Personenverkehr AG (CC BY 4.0); data source: Mobilitätsverbünde Österreich OG, data.mobilitaetsverbuende.at.

GET /v1/weather/nowcast/{coordinates}
GeoSphere INCA nowcast nowcast-v1-15min-1km (a new analysis every 15 min), bilinear to the point. The horizon ends 3 h after reference_time (the analysis); because a run is published 20 to 40 minutes after its analysis time, the steps reach about 2 to 2.5 h ahead of now, see valid_until.

GET /v1/weather/tiles/{param}/{time}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png
Color ramp per parameter (see legend in the TileJSON). time: now or a time such as 2026-11-07T20:00:00Z (a UTC offset such as +01:00 is allowed, URL-encode + as %2B); it snaps to the nearest step within 30 minutes, the step actually used is in the header X-Weather-Time.

data: Validation compares the four address parts with the BEV address register. The result has a status (match, corrected, ambiguous, not_found), the list of deviations and either the matching address with coordinates or a list of candidates. The pre-filled address has a typo on purpose. MapLibre GL JSOpenLayersLeaflet Validate Press Validate. The map needs JavaScript. data:
The streets style contains an extruded building layer that is switched off by default. The layer ids are listed in the style metadata (mapx:groups), so you switch a whole group on without knowing the names. Zoom in to level 15 or more and tilt the map (right mouse button or two fingers).
3D buildings are only available in MapLibre; OpenLayers and Leaflet draw flat maps.
The map needs JavaScript. Code import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs"; // 3D buildings: switch on the extruded building layer of the streets style and tilt the camera. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets', center: [16.3725, 48.2085], zoom: 16.2, pitch: 62, bearing: -20 }); // Stephansplatz, Vienna map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once('load', () => map.getContainer().querySelector('.maplibregl-compact-show')?.classList.remove('maplibregl-compact-show')); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) map.on('style.load', () => { // The style lists its layer groups in the metadata, so no layer names are hard-coded. for (const id of map.getStyle().metadata['mapx:groups'].buildings3d) map.setLayoutProperty(id, 'visibility', 'visible'); }); Complete HTML file Save and open in a browser. data: The optimization finds the best order for a round trip. Here the vehicle starts and ends in Melk. Click up to nine stops; every click plans again. The example uses GET /v1/optimized-trips/driving/{coordinates} with source=first and roundtrip=true; it works with a public token, and the response contains the order and the route. For several vehicles, service times, capacities and time windows there is POST /v1/optimization. It needs a secret token (mx_sk_…); a public token gets 403 pk-not-allowed. Send that request through your own server, not straight from the web page. MapLibre GL JSOpenLayersLeaflet Start over Click at least two stops. The map needs JavaScript. Code MapLibre GL JSOpenLayersLeaflet MapLibre GL JS import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs"; // Tour planning: click stops (up to 9), the optimized-trips API finds the shortest order from the depot and back. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); // Note: the richer POST /v1/optimization (time windows, capacities) needs a secret token (mx_sk_…); call it from your server. const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; const de = document.documentElement.lang.startsWith('de'); // page language: German or English texts maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const depot = [15.3294, 48.2272]; // Melk const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets', center: depot, zoom: 9 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once('load', () => map.getContainer().querySelector('.maplibregl-compact-show')?.classList.remove('maplibregl-compact-show')); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) const stops = [], markers = []; let timer; new maplibregl.Marker({ color: '#222' }).setLngLat(depot).addTo(map); map.on('load', () => { map.addSource('tour', { type: 'geojson', data: { type: 'FeatureCollection', features: [] } }); map.addLayer({ id: 'tour', type: 'line', source: 'tour', layout: { 'line-cap': 'round', 'line-join': 'round' }, paint: { 'line-color': '#2346d8', 'line-width': 5 } }); }); map.on('click', (e) => { if (stops.length >= 9) return; stops.push([e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat]); markers.push(new maplibregl.Marker({ color: '#c8372d' }).setLngLat(e.lngLat).addTo(map)); clearTimeout(timer); // plan once after the last click if (stops.length >= 2) timer = setTimeout(plan, 600); }); document.getElementById('reset').addEventListener('click', () => { stops.length = 0; markers.splice(0).forEach((m) => m.remove()); map.getSource('tour').setData({ type: 'FeatureCollection', features: [] }); document.getElementById('info').textContent = de ? data: The TileJSON /v1/weather/tiles/rr_nowcast.json lists the 15-minute steps under mapx:time.times. The example adds one raster layer per step and switches their visibility, so the animation does not wait for tiles. For a single point use GET /v1/weather/nowcast/{lon},{lat}. OpenLayers loads a layer only once it becomes visible: the OpenLayers version fetches each step when first shown, later it comes from the cache. Search Box works in two steps: suggest returns suggestions while the user types, retrieve returns the position of the chosen one. Use the same session_token for both calls and a new one for the next search. The type filter limits the suggestions.

One session token per search. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? data: A static image is a plain URL that returns a PNG or WebP: for real-estate listings, e-mails, PDFs and places without JavaScript. Style, pin, view and size are part of the path. Click the map to move the pin; the image below is the URL shown under it. A static image is just an image URL, so no map library is needed; the map here only picks the place. data:
One TileJSON URL per product is enough: MapLibre reads tile URL, zoom range and attribution from it. Here a custom, minimal style. OpenLayers does not read TileJSON for vector tiles itself: the OpenLayers version loads it with fetch and builds ol.source.XYZ (raster) and ol.source.VectorTile with ol.format.MVT (vector tiles) from it.
MapLibre GL JSOpenLayersLeaflet Leaflet shows only the raster part: it has no vector tiles without a plugin, so the contour lines are missing there.
The map needs JavaScript. '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, transformRequest, container: 'map', center: [11.4, 47.27], zoom: 12.5, // Innsbruck style: { version: 8, sources: { ortho: { type: 'raster', url: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/tiles/orthophoto.json', tileSize: 512 }, linien: { type: 'vector', url: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/tiles/contours.json' }, }, layers: [ { id: 'ortho', type: 'raster', source: 'ortho' }, { id: 'linien', type: 'line', source: 'linien', 'source-layer': 'contour_l', paint: { 'line-color': '#ffd24a', 'line-width': 0.8, 'line-opacity': 0.9 } }, ], }, }); '', 'text/html').body.textContent; L.tileLayer(tj.tiles[0] + '?access_token=' + TOKEN, { tileSize: 512, zoomOffset: -1, minZoom: tj.minzoom + 1, maxNativeZoom: tj.maxzoom + 1, maxZoom: 21, attribution: Object.assign(document.createElement('span'), { textContent: plain }).innerHTML }).addTo(map); })(); Complete HTML file MapLibre GL JS Save and open in a browser. /examples/time-of-day/.title: Time of day and night mode example

data: The style traffic-day shows the current reports and colours the motorway sections where variable message signs limit the speed; there is no area-wide traffic flow. Incidents (accidents, roadworks, closures) come from /v1/traffic/incidents; the example loads the active ones for the visible area and draws them on top. Click a line for the text. MapLibre GL JSOpenLayersLeaflet The map needs JavaScript. Code MapLibre GL JSOpenLayersLeaflet MapLibre GL JS import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs"; // Traffic: the traffic-day style (reports, sign speed limits on motorways) plus the current incident list for the visible area. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, transformRequest, container: 'map', style: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/traffic-day', center: [16.2, 48.1], zoom: 9 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once('load', () => map.getContainer().querySelector('.maplibregl-compact-show')?.classList.remove('maplibregl-compact-show')); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) const list = document.getElementById('meldungen'); const popup = new maplibregl.Popup(); map.on('load', () => { map.addSource('incidents', { type: 'geojson', data: { type: 'FeatureCollection', features: [] } }); map.addLayer({ id: 'incidents', type: 'line', source: 'incidents', layout: { 'line-cap': 'round' }, paint: { 'line-color': ['case', ['get', 'closed'], '#c8372d', '#e8890c'], 'line-width': 6, 'line-opacity': 0.8 } }); map.on('click', 'incidents', (e) => popup.setLngLat(e.lngLat).setText(e.features[0].properties.text).addTo(map)); const load = async () => { const b = map.getBounds(); const res = await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?bbox=${b.getWest()},${b.getSouth()},${b.getEast()},${b.getNorth()}&active=true&limit=50`, AUTH); const fc = await res.json(); map.getSource('incidents').setData(fc); const de = document.documentElement.lang.startsWith('de'); // page language: German or English text const first = fc.features[0] ? `${fc.features[0].properties.road ?? ''} ${fc.features[0].properties.type}` : ''; list.textContent = de ? `${fc.features.length} aktive Meldung(en) im Ausschnitt` + (first ? `, z. B. ${first}` : '') : `${fc.features.length} active incident(s) in view` + (first ? `, e.g. ${first}` : ''); }; map.on('moveend', load); load(); }); OpenLayers // Traffic: the current incident list for the visible area on the street map (the traffic-day style has no raster tiles). const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; // Data sources (CC BY 4.0), must stay visible on the map; full text per source: https://docs.mapx.at/reference/attribution/ const ATTRIBUTION = 'mapx.at, BEV, GIP.at; Verkehr/traffic: ASFINAG, EVIS.AT; CC BY 4.0'; const base = new ol.layer.Tile({ source: new ol.source.XYZ({ url: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets/tiles/512/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=' + TOKEN, tileSize: 512, maxZoom: 20, attributions: ATTRIBUTION, attributionsCollapsible: false }) }); const incidents = new ol.source.Vector(); const style = (f) => new ol.style.Style({ stroke: new ol.style.Stroke({ color: f.get('closed') ? 'rgba(200, 55, 45, 0.8)' : 'rgba(232, 137, 12, 0.8)', width: 6, lineCap: 'round' }) }); const label = document.createElement('div'); // OpenLayers has no popup of its own: an overlay with a plain element label.style.cssText = 'background:#fff;color:#000;padding:4px 8px;border-radius:6px;font:13px system-ui,sans-serif;box-shadow:0 1px 4px #0006'; const popup = new ol.Overlay({ element: label, positioning: 'bottom-center', offset: [0, -8] }); const map = new ol.Map({ target: 'map', layers: [base, new ol.layer.Vector({ source: incidents, style })], overlays: [popup], view: new ol.View({ center: ol.proj.fromLonLat([16.2, 48.1]), zoom: 10 }) }); const geojson = new ol.format.GeoJSON({ featureProjection: 'EPSG:3857' }); // reads lon/lat GeoJSON into map coordinates const list = document.getElementById('meldungen'); map.on('click', (e) => { const f = map.forEachFeatureAtPixel(e.pixel, (x) => x, { hitTolerance: 4 }); label.textContent = f?.get('text') ?? ''; popup.setPosition(f ? e.coordinate : undefined); }); map.on('moveend', async () => { const [w, s, e, n] = ol.proj.transformExtent(map.getView().calculateExtent(map.getSize()), 'EPSG:3857', 'EPSG:4326'); const de = document.documentElement.lang.startsWith('de'); // page language: German or English text try { const res = await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?bbox=${w},${s},${e},${n}&active=true&limit=50`, AUTH); if (!res.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status); const fc = await res.json(); incidents.clear(); incidents.addFeatures(geojson.readFeatures(fc)); const first = fc.features[0] ? `${fc.features[0].properties.road ?? ''} ${fc.features[0].properties.type}` : ''; list.textContent = de ? `${fc.features.length} aktive Meldung(en) im Ausschnitt` + (first ? `, z. B. ${first}` : '') : `${fc.features.length} active incident(s) in view` + (first ? `, e.g. ${first}` : ''); } catch (err) { list.textContent = (de ? 'Fehler: ' : 'Error: ') + err.message; } }); Leaflet // Traffic: the current incident list of the visible area as lines over the map, closures in red, a click shows the report. // The traffic-day style (sign speed limits, traffic layers) has no raster tiles, so the streets style is the basemap here. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; const de = document.documentElement.lang.startsWith('de'); // page language: German or English texts // Data sources of the style and the traffic data (CC BY 4.0), must stay visible on the map; full text per source: https://docs.mapx.at/reference/attribution/ const ATTRIBUTION = 'mapx.at, BEV, GIP.at, Verkehr: ASFINAG / EVIS.AT, CC BY 4.0'; const map = L.map('map').setView([48.1, 16.2], 10); L.tileLayer('https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets/tiles/512/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=' + TOKEN, { tileSize: 512, zoomOffset: -1, minZoom: 1, maxZoom: 21, attribution: ATTRIBUTION }).addTo(map); const list = document.getElementById('meldungen'); const popup = L.popup(); const incidents = L.geoJSON(null, { style: (f) => ({ color: f.properties.closed ? In OpenLayers, each hour is its own ol.source.XYZ. MapLibre GL JSOpenLayersLeaflet Quantity TemperaturePrecipitationWindCloud cover Hour Loading … The map needs JavaScript. Code MapLibre GL JSOpenLayersLeaflet MapLibre GL JS import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs"; // Weather overlay: temperature (or precipitation, wind ...) as raster tiles over the map, hour selectable. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; // your public token (mx_pk_…) from https://account.mapx.at // Adds the token to every request MapLibre makes to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites), never to other hosts. const transformRequest = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) ? url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'access_token=' + TOKEN : url }); const AUTH = { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } }; maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const API = 'https://api.mapx.at/v1'; const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, transformRequest, container: 'map', style: API + '/styles/streets', center: [13.3, 47.6], zoom: 6.5 }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once('load', () => map.getContainer().querySelector('.maplibregl-compact-show')?.classList.remove('maplibregl-compact-show')); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) let times = []; async function laden() { const param = document.getElementById('param').value; // temperature, precipitation, wind ... const tj = await (await fetch(`${API}/weather/tiles/${param}.json`, AUTH)).json(); times = tj['mapx:time'].times; // available hours (UTC) const slider = document.getElementById('stunde'); slider.max = times.length - 1; zeigen(param, Number(slider.value)); } function zeigen(param, i) { const t = times[Math.min(i, times.length - 1)]; const source = document.documentElement.lang.startsWith('de') ? 'Quelle' : 'Source'; // page language document.getElementById('info').textContent = `${param}, ${t} (UTC), ${source}: GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0`; if (map.getLayer('wetter')) map.removeLayer('wetter'); if (map.getSource('wetter')) map.removeSource('wetter'); map.addSource('wetter', { type: 'raster', tileSize: 512, maxzoom: 11, // smooth fields: fewer, larger tiles keep the request count low tiles: [`${API}/weather/tiles/${param}/${t}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`], attribution: 'Wetter: GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0', }); map.addLayer({ id: 'wetter', type: 'raster', source: 'wetter', paint: { 'raster-opacity': 0.85, 'raster-fade-duration': 0 } }); } map.on('load', laden); document.getElementById('param').addEventListener('change', () => { document.getElementById('stunde').value = 0; laden(); }); document.getElementById('stunde').addEventListener('input', (e) => zeigen(document.getElementById('param').value, Number(e.target.value))); OpenLayers // Weather overlay: temperature (or precipitation, wind ...) as raster tiles over the map, hour selectable. const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; data:
Goal: A map where the orthophoto is draped over real terrain, shaded for depth and tiltable in the browser.
Prerequisites: a browser and any static web server (for example npx serve). A free API token (Access and limits).
This guide uses the DTM (elevation, type raster-dem) and the orthophoto (imagery, type raster). Both tilesets are added via TileJSON, so you never need a file name.
Create the page. A file index.html with MapLibre GL JS and a map container:
<meta charset="utf-8"> <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.css"> <style>html, body, #map { margin: 0; height: 100%; }style> <div id="map">div> Declare the sources. The elevation model as raster-dem (twice: one source for the terrain, one for the hillshade, which renders better), the orthophoto as raster. Plus the token, which is added to every request to mapx.at:
const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… // adds the token to every request to mapx.at (TileJSON and tiles) const withToken = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) && !url.includes("access_token=") ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url }); const sources = { dem: { type: "raster-dem", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb.json", encoding: "mapbox" }, "dem-hillshade": { type: "raster-dem", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb.json", encoding: "mapbox" }, ortho: { type: "raster", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/orthophoto.json", tileSize: 512 } }; Stack the layers. Imagery at the bottom, hillshade on top with a light touch so the photo stays recognisable:
const layers = [ { id: "ortho", type: "raster", source: "ortho" }, { id: "hillshade", type: "hillshade", source: "dem-hillshade", paint: { "hillshade-exaggeration": 0.4, "hillshade-shadow-color": "#000000" } } ]; Enable terrain. terrain lifts all layers to the DTM elevation. pitch tilts the view:
<script type="module"> import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs"; const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, container: "map", transformRequest: withToken, center: [12.694, 47.074], zoom: 12, pitch: 65, bearing: 20, maxPitch: 80, style: { version: 8, sources: sources, layers: layers, terrain: { source: "dem", exaggeration: 1.3 } } }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once("load", () => map.getContainer().querySelector(".maplibregl-compact-show")?.classList.remove("maplibregl-compact-show")); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl({ visualizePitch: true })); script> The constants from steps 2 and 3 (TOKEN, withToken, sources, layers) must appear in the same
data.next-steps#Next steps: Read the elevation at a click: map.queryTerrainElevation(e.lngLat), details in DTM terrain model. Contour lines and labels on top: Overlay contour lines. Elevation profile along a line: Elevation profile. Show the credit correctly: Attribution.
data.result#Result:
The aerial imagery lies on the terrain around the Großglockner, slopes are additionally shaded. The orthophoto reaches z18 (20 cm), the DTM z16 (1 m raster); MapLibre scales up automatically beyond that.
exaggeration exaggerates the relief. 1.0 is natural; for flat terrain 1.5 to 2 looks more plastic.

data:
Goal: Query an elevation profile (distance against elevation) for a route and draw it as a chart. Prerequisites: a browser. A free token (Access and limits), no framework, no library. With path and samples, the /v1/elevation endpoint returns elevation values spaced evenly by length along the line. If you only need the finished totals (ascent, descent, lowest and highest point), use /v1/elevation/profile; here the profile is computed and drawn by hand. Test the request. The line is made of lon,lat pairs separated by semicolons (longitude first). 50 sample points along a route at the Großglockner: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation?path=12.69,47.07;12.70,47.08&samples=50" The response is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, one feature per sample with elevation (m) and distance_m (distance from the start). Create the page. A file profile.html with an empty SVG:

p> Load and draw the profile. The script fetches the data, scales distance and elevation to the canvas and builds a line with a filled area below:
data.next-steps#Next steps: All parameters and response fields: Elevation and profile. Line from a GPX track: join the coordinates as lon,lat;lon,lat, order see Coordinates. Limits for many requests: Errors and limits.
data.result#Result:
An SVG chart with area and line of elevation over distance, with length, ascent and descent below.
The simple sum in this example grows with samples, because it adds up terrain noise. /v1/elevation/profile counts ascent and descent with a 3 m hysteresis instead, which hardly depends on samples; use its ascent_m and descent_m when you show totals. With model=dsm the profile follows the surface (trees, buildings) instead of the ground, see DTM and DSM. A path has 2 to 512 vertices, samples 2 to 1024.

data: mapx has two height models of 1 m resolution (BEV, laser scanning): the terrain model dtm (bare ground) and the surface model dsm (including trees and buildings). Use dtm for gradients, profiles and trails, dsm for visibility and building heights. Every request needs a token (Access and limits); the samples send it in the Authorization header, which browsers may send too.
data.3d-terrain-in-the-map#3D terrain in the:
Add the terrain-rgb tileset as raster-dem source and turn on terrain:
map.on("load", () => { // two separate sources: one for the terrain, one for the hillshade (better rendering) map.addSource("dem", { type: "raster-dem", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb.json", tileSize: 512 }); map.addSource("dem-hillshade", { type: "raster-dem", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb.json", tileSize: 512 }); map.setTerrain({ source: "dem", exaggeration: 1.2 }); map.addLayer({ id: "hillshade", type: "hillshade", source: "dem-hillshade" }); map.setPitch(60); }); Step-by-step with aerial imagery: 3D terrain with orthophoto. The style outdoors already includes hillshade and contours; the ready-made 3D styles outdoors-3d and satellite-3d bring the terrain along, see Maps.
data.elevation-profile#Elevation profile:
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation/profile?coordinates=12.69,47.07;12.72,47.09&samples=50"; const { properties: p } = await (await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); console.log(p.ascent_m, p.descent_m, p.min_m, p.max_m); // p.distances[i] (m from the start) and p.elevations[i] (m) are ready for a chart Up to 1024 samples along a line of 2 to 512 vertices. Ascent and descent are counted with a 3 m hysteresis (ascent_threshold_m): a rise or fall counts only once the elevation has moved at least 3 m from the last turning point, so terrain noise does not add up and the totals hardly depend on samples. With model=dsm trees and buildings count as terrain and the ascent comes out higher.
A route geometry goes straight into the profile with POST /v1/elevation/profile (GeoJSON LineString, a Feature or {"coordinates": [...]}, up to 20000 vertices):
const route = (await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/cycling/12.8418,47.0378;12.7303,47.0792?geometries=geojson&overview=full", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json()).routes[0]; const prof = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation/profile?samples=200", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN", "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(route.geometry), })).json(); console.log(prof.properties.ascent_m); Example with a chart: Elevation profile. Routes already carry ascent and descent in routes[].summary; use annotations=elevation for a height per segment.
data.height-at-a-point#Height at a point:
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation/12.694,47.074" | jq '.properties | {dtm, dsm}' Several points, up to 512, in one request:
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation?points=12.694,47.074;15.3294,48.2272&model=dtm"; const { features } = await (await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); console.log(features.map((f) => f.properties.elevation)); // meters above sea level Heights are in meters with 0.1 m steps. Outside the data area the value is null.
data.next#Next: Elevation API Tilesets: terrain model data sheet Overlay contour lines
data.read-heights-from-tiles#Read heights fro: The tiles use the Terrain-RGB encoding: height = -10000 + (R * 65536 + G * 256 + B) * 0.1. Decode tiles yourself for bulk work, see Terrain-RGB. For single points the API is simpler.
