data: Goal: a mapx map in an existing Leaflet application (1.9.4), no build and no plugin, with a free public token (see Access and limits).
data.add-the-basemap#Add the basemap:
Leaflet does not draw vector tiles. The mapx styles are therefore also available rendered as raster tiles (Static Tiles), added with L.tileLayer. The tiles are 512 pixels: tileSize: 512 and zoomOffset: -1 keep the scale of ordinary 256 pixel tiles. Styles: streets (and variants), light, dark, satellite, satellite-streets, outdoors, outdoors-winter; not available as raster tiles are traffic-day, traffic-night, satellite-current, the relief styles and the -3d styles.
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css"> <script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js">script> <div id="map" style="height:70vh">div> <script> const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; const map = L.map('map').setView([48.21, 16.37], 13); L.tileLayer('https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets/tiles/512/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=' + TOKEN, { tileSize: 512, zoomOffset: -1, minZoom: 1, maxZoom: 21, attribution: 'mapx.at, BEV, GIP.at, CC BY 4.0', }).addTo(map); script> The token goes into the tile URL as access_token; API calls with fetch send it as the header Authorization: Bearer ….
data.attribution#Attribution: The data is licensed CC BY 4.0 and users must be able to reach the source on the map. Leaflet shows the attribution text in the bottom right corner; the text per source is listed in Attribution and license.
data.examples#Examples: Examples with a Leaflet version are listed in the overview (filter “Leaflet”), for instance Embed a map and Route.
data.limits#Limits: No vector style: the basemap arrives as an image, labels and layers cannot be changed one by one. Use MapLibre for that. No 3D terrain and no 3D buildings, these are only available in MapLibre. Raster tiles count in the rate limit zone static (5 requests per second per IP address, briefly up to 60 at once, plus the per-minute limit of 6000 per token, see Access and limits). Ordinary panning and zooming stays well below that; only requesting new tiles faster for a sustained period returns 429.
data.your-own-geojson#Your own GeoJSON:
API responses (route, isochrone …) are GeoJSON and go straight into L.geoJSON:
const layer = L.geoJSON(null, { style: { color: '#2346d8', weight: 4 } }).addTo(map); layer.addData(geojson);

data:
mapx delivers maps as ready-made styles and as tiles. Use a style to get a complete map in one line; use tilesets when you build your own style.
Before you start: a page with MapLibre GL JS, see First map. You need a free token (Access and limits); the snippets show YOUR_TOKEN only where it matters. The style example shows the handover with transformRequest; the later snippets assume it.
PMTiles protocol: the mapx styles load their tiles from PMTiles files. The page must therefore include pmtiles.js and call maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new pmtiles.Protocol().tile) once; otherwise the map stays empty (console: URL scheme "pmtiles" is not supported). All snippets below assume it. Your own styles that only use TileJSON sources (https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/{tileset}.json) do not need it.
data.3d-styles#3D styles:
Style Content outdoors-3d, outdoors-winter-3d, relief-3d outdoors, outdoors-winter or relief draped over the real terrain model, with sky and horizon satellite-3d, satellite-streets-3d Aerial imagery over the terrain, plain or with roads and names streets-3d, streets-night-3d City map with extruded buildings (heights from the BEV building model) and scene lighting, by day or by night light-3d, dark-3d Quiet light or dark base map with grey or anthracite buildings, for your own data The 3D styles turn on the sky (sky) and the terrain (terrain on the terrain model terrain-rgb, without exaggeration in the city styles) in the style and come with a tilted start view (pitch 72, city 68, plus bearing). MapLibre takes pitch and bearing from the style only when the map is created without a camera position; when you pass center and zoom, also pass pitch and bearing. By default MapLibre allows at most 60 degrees of pitch, which usually keeps the horizon out of view. To see the sky, set maxPitch and pitch yourself:
maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); // once per page, see above const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: "map", style: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets-3d", // transformRequest as in the snippet further down center: [16.3731, 48.2085], zoom: 15, maxPitch: 78, pitch: 74, bearing: -20, // the sky comes into view from about 72 degrees of pitch }); // City styles: buildings up to the horizon (set again after every style load) map.on("style.load", () => map.setSourceTileLodParams(3, 6)); At a steep pitch MapLibre loads tiles of lower zoom levels for the distance. Below zoom 12 they contain no buildings, so the building bodies stop in the background. setSourceTileLodParams(3, 6) limits the number of zoom levels in view to three, so the bodies reach the horizon; the map loads a few more tiles in return. The terrain and aerial styles do not need this.
Keep maxPitch at 78 or below in the city styles: at a steeper pitch MapLibre cuts the terrain off at the horizon but still draws the buildings on hills behind it, so they appear to float.
Buildings appear as bodies from about zoom 13 (merged buildings with an average height, from zoom 15 every building with its own height). Heights come from the BEV building model, missing ones from the elevation models (surface minus terrain); tall towers are separate parts (building_part_a) on top of the buildings. Terrain covers Austria only. The 3D styles exist only for maps in the browser (MapLibre GL JS), not as static images or static tiles; use the style without -3d there (there is no image for relief-3d either).
const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); // the styles load PMTiles const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, container: "map", style: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/outdoors", // adds the token to every request to mapx.at transformRequest: (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) && !url.includes("access_token=") ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url, }), center: [12.694, 47.074], zoom: 12, // Grossglockner }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once("load", () => map.getContainer().querySelector(".maplibregl-compact-show")?.classList.remove("maplibregl-compact-show")); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) Switching style at runtime replaces layers and sources: call map.setStyle(url). Add your own sources and layers again afterwards (for example in the style.load event). See Switch the basemap.
data.add-tilesets-to-your-own-style#Add tiles:
Every tileset has a TileJSON address https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/{tileset}.json. MapLibre reads zoom range, bounds and attribution from it.
Tileset Type Content streets vector Roads, rail, water, boundaries, places, buildings contours vector Contour lines terrain-rgb, dsm raster-dem Terrain and surface height orthophoto raster Aerial photo, up to z18 map.on("load", () => { map.addSource("mx-contours", { type: "vector", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/contours.json" }); map.addLayer({ id: "mx-contours", type: "line", source: "mx-contours", "source-layer": "contour_l", paint: { "line-color": "#92400e", "line-width": 0.6 } }); }); The mapx styles already use the source names streets, contours, terrain-rgb, dsm, orthophoto, traffic and others. Pick your own name when you add a source to a mapx style (here mx-contours); outdoors already shows contour lines. Layer names and fields: Tilesets. Add your own data the same way with a geojson source; a complete example is GeoJSON overlay.
data.next#Next: Style the basemap Tilesets Styles API and Tiles API
data.offline-and-bulk-use#Offline and bulk us:
Tiles and tilesets are available only through the API: style, TileJSON or {z}/{x}/{y}. mapx does not offer whole files for download. For many requests, cache tiles in the client, see Access and limits.
Show the data source on the map. MapLibre does this automatically when you load a style or TileJSON, with mapx.at (link) as the first entry; please do not remove it; the code above collapses it behind the “i” button, see Attribution.
data.other-clients#Other clients:
The TileJSON format works in MapLibre and QGIS. The styles themselves load PMTiles files (pmtiles://) and therefore run only in clients that know this protocol, such as MapLibre with pmtiles.js. For clients without vector support, Static Tiles deliver the rendered style as raster tiles; this is how OpenLayers and Leaflet add the basemap:
https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets/tiles/512/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN
data.use-a-style#Use a style:
Style Look streets Base map, roads, places, buildings streets-dawn, streets-dusk, streets-night The same map in other light satellite Orthophoto satellite-current Current satellite image (Sentinel-2) instead of the orthophoto satellite-streets Orthophoto with roads and labels light, dark Calm, almost monochrome base map (light or dark) for your own data outdoors Contours, hillshade, trails outdoors-winter Like outdoors in snow colours, ski areas and cable cars/lifts highlighted relief Pure relief map: elevation tints from green valleys through yellow, ochre and brown to grey and white at the peaks, strong hillshade, lakes and rivers, a few names (places, peaks with height, water); no roads or buildings relief-contours Like relief, with contour lines and their heights relief-light, relief-dark Grey hillshade only on a light or dark background, very restrained, a backdrop for your own data traffic-day, traffic-night Map with the current traffic reports and closures (day or night), see Traffic The relief styles need MapLibre GL JS 5.6 or later (layer type color-relief) and exist only for maps in the browser. They show Austria only (terrain model BEV ALS-DTM 1 m, z5 to z16); the area outside stays plain.
As an image: Static images and Static Tiles render streets (with the time-of-day variants), light, dark, satellite, satellite-streets, outdoors (the full vector map) and outdoors-winter. Not available as an image are traffic-day and traffic-night (answer 404 with a hint to use streets or streets-night), satellite-current, the relief styles and all -3d styles.
data.weather-and-traffic-overlays#Weather and:
Raster weather tiles have a time dimension; the TileJSON of temperature, precipitation, wind, humidity, cloud or pressure lists the available times in the field mapx:time.times. The tile URL contains /now/ by default; to choose another time, put an entry of that list in place of now (template in mapx:time.template). The same URL scheme serves the air quality layers aqi (daily index), no2, o3, pm10, pm25 and dust (Saharan dust), see Air Quality API.
map.addSource("temp", { type: "raster", url: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/weather/tiles/temperature.json", tileSize: 256 }); map.addLayer({ id: "temp", type: "raster", source: "temp", paint: { "raster-opacity": 0.6 } }); The traffic layer is a vector source, see Traffic. Example: Weather overlay.

/guides/maps/.title: Maps guide: vector tiles and styles

data:
The mapx MCP server gives an AI assistant 21 tools for Austrian geodata: address search, routes, public transport, heights, traffic and weather. It uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so any MCP client can connect. All tools are read-only, the data covers Austria only and comes from official open data, and every answer names its source.
Property Value Endpoint https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp Transport Streamable HTTP, POST only, stateless Protocol versions 2026-07-28 and older ones from 2024-11-05 Authentication Either sign in with your mapx account (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, just enter the address) or a token of type “AI assistant (MCP)”, prefix mx_mcp_, in the header Authorization: Bearer …
data.clients-for-the-token-way#Clients for th:
These clients take a fixed header, so the token goes straight into the configuration.
Claude CodeCursorVS CodeGemini CLIAnthropic APIOpenAI API claude mcp add --transport http mapx https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" In mcp.json:
{ "mcpServers": { "mapx": { "url": "https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" } } } } In .vscode/mcp.json:
{ "servers": { "mapx": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" } } } } In settings.json:
{ "mcpServers": { "mapx": { "httpUrl": "https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" } } } } The MCP connector of the Messages API is in beta; the beta header and model name below are those of its documentation at the time of writing, so check them there.
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2026-10-21" \ -H "anthropic-beta: mcp-client-2025-11-20" \ -d '{ "model": "claude-opus-5-5", "max_tokens": 1000, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "How long does a truck take from Vienna to Linz?"}], "mcp_servers": [ { "type": "url", "url": "https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp", "name": "mapx", "authorization_token": "YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" } ], "tools": [ { "type": "mcp_toolset", "mcp_server_name": "mapx" } ] }' The remote MCP tool of the Responses API. OpenAI asks for approval before data is sent to the server unless you set require_approval. The authorization value is not stored, so send it with every request.
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "model": "YOUR_MODEL", "input": "How long does a truck take from Vienna to Linz?", "tools": [ { "type": "mcp", "server_label": "mapx", "server_url": "https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp", "authorization": "YOUR_MCP_TOKEN" } ] }'
data.disconnect#Disconnect: At account.mapx.at → Tokens every connection made through your account is listed as “connected via ”. Disconnect ends it; Block rejects it immediately and can be undone. The assistant then gets 401 and asks you to sign in again when needed.
data.errors#Errors: The assistant receives the error as text and can react to it. Error codes and causes are listed in Errors and limits, in particular mcp-token-only and mcp-token-required.
data.example-questions#Example questions: “Where is Herrengasse 13 in 1010 Vienna, and where is the nearest fuel station?” “How long does a truck with 40 t take from Vienna to Linz, and are there closures on the way?” “Which parts of Melk can I reach within 15 minutes on foot from the station?” “What are the next departures at Melk Bahnhof?” “How high is the Grossglockner area, and what does the profile of my hiking path look like?” “Will it rain in Innsbruck in the next three hours?” “Plan the best order for these five delivery addresses and show them on a map.”
data.for-developers#For developers:
The MCP server follows MCP authorization (OAuth 2.1):
Protected resource metadata: https://mcp.mapx.at/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp Authorization server: https://account.mapx.at (metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) Authorization code with PKCE (S256); public clients identify themselves through Client ID Metadata Documents, there is no dynamic registration. Scope mcp. The access token does not expire and there is no refresh token; revocation happens in the account. Limits, counting and tools are the same for both ways.
data.limitations#Limitations: Austria only; data comes from official open data, and each answer names the source. All tools only read; nothing is changed or stored. Public transport answers come from the scheduled timetable, from the scheduled timetable. Climate, weather, warnings and air quality come from GeoSphere Austria, traffic reports from ASFINAG and EVIS.AT. Long results are shortened.
data.limits-and-counting#Limits and counting: Every tool call counts like an API call and appears in your usage view as MCP. Some tools make several API calls, for example free-text search in search_places (up to 11). The protocol messages themselves (each request to /mcp) are listed separately as product mcp; they do not use up the per-minute limit. The per-minute limit of your token (6000 by default) and the zone limits of the API apply, over MCP per token instead of per IP address (Access and limits). The MCP endpoint itself accepts 10 requests per second per IP address (burst 40) and request bodies up to 256 KB. Per token, at most 4 calls run at the same time; further ones wait or fail with a waiting time. If a limit is exceeded, the assistant gets an error message with a waiting time.
data.next#Next: Access and limits Errors and limits
data.privacy#Privacy: Your questions and the results pass through the provider of your assistant. mapx only sees the tool calls, like ordinary API calls.
data.set-up#Set up: There are two ways. Signing in with your account is the simpler one: you only enter the address and do not copy a token. The token way works with any MCP client.
data.sign-in-with-your-account#Sign in with y:
Add https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp as an MCP server in your application (see below). The assistant sends you to account.mapx.at. Sign in with your e-mail address; without an account you create one after entering the code. The consent page shows the application, the redirect target, your account and what the access allows: read-only tools only, calls count towards your usage, no access to your account or your other tokens. Confirm the connection. Ask a question that needs Austrian data, for example “How do I get by bike from Melk station to Melk Abbey, and how long does it take?”. The connection then appears at account.mapx.at → Tokens as “connected via ”. Each application can hold up to five connections at the same time, for example browser, desktop and phone. The connection does not expire on its own.
These applications are approved for signing in with your account:
claude.ai (web, desktop, mobile): under Connectors in the settings, add a custom connector and enter the address. The exact menu path depends on your plan and changes over time; it is described in Anthropic’s help. On Team and Enterprise plans an owner adds the connector first. Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http mapx https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp, then enter /mcp in Claude Code and start the sign-in for mapx. ChatGPT: connectors or apps with your own MCP address, available depending on plan and settings (sometimes only in developer mode). Steps and availability are in OpenAI’s help. Signing in with your account is limited to known applications. For all other clients use the token way; further applications can be enabled on request (support@mapx.at).
data.tools#Tools:
The assistant picks the tools itself. Coordinates are {lon, lat} in WGS84; geocode turns a place name into coordinates for the other tools.
Group Tool Purpose Main inputs Search geocode Coordinates for an address, street, place, postcode, POI or road kilometer query, near, types, limit Search reverse_geocode Nearest address or place for a coordinate lon, lat, radius_m, types Search validate_address Check an address against the official register and normalize it address or street, housenumber, postcode, place Search search_places Points of interest by category or name category, query, near, near_place, radius_m, limit Search list_place_categories Category ids usable in search_places none Routing route Route by car, truck, bike or on foot with distance, time and instructions profile, waypoints (2 to 25), exclude, truck Routing isochrone Area reachable within given minutes or meters profile, lon, lat, minutes, meters, depart_at Routing travel_matrix Travel times between 2 to 25 points profile, points, sources, destinations Routing optimize_stops Fastest order of 2 to 25 stops profile, stops, roundtrip, start, end Public transport transit_route Connections between two points from the scheduled timetable from, to, depart_at, arrive_by, access, connections Public transport departures Next scheduled departures at a stop or around a point stop_id or near, time, limit Public transport find_stops Stops near a point or in a box, with stop_id near, radius_m, bbox, limit Elevation elevation Height above sea level (terrain or surface model) points, model Elevation elevation_profile Ascent, descent, lowest and highest point along a line path (2 to 200 points), samples, model Traffic traffic_incidents Accidents, congestion, roadworks and closures bbox, road, road_class, types, planned Traffic speed_limits Statutory speed limits at a point, in a box or along a path at, bbox, path, buffer_m Weather weather Current observations, hourly forecast or nowcast lon, lat, kind, hours Weather weather_warnings Official weather warnings at, bbox, type, min_level, active_now Weather climate Long-term climate facts, solar potential lon, lat, sections Weather air_quality Air quality index and pollutants lon, lat, hours Map static_map Map image with pins and a line center, zoom, pins, line, style, width, height search_places with free text and near searches only within radius_m (500 to 100000 meters, default 25000), sorts by distance and says so explicitly when it has to fall back to matches farther away. A category search always returns the nearest first and ignores radius_m. Instead of the coordinate near you can pass a place name or address as near_place (for example “Melk”); the server resolves it with one additional API call, takes the first match and states in the result which place it searched around and which other matches there were. The place search returns name, type, coordinates and distance, but no opening hours, phone numbers or reviews.
Times in the answer text are Austrian local time with the offset, for example 2026-11-18T08:00+01:00; this applies to weather, warnings, air quality and traffic reports. Public transport times are local time as well. The structured part of the result (structuredContent) keeps the timestamps of the API.
Routing profiles are driving, driving-traffic, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb and walking; isochrone also accepts transit.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause and fix 401 No or invalid token. With sign-in through your account, this makes the assistant start the sign-in; after you disconnect or block the connection it reports 401 and asks again. With the token way, check the Authorization: Bearer header and that the token was not deleted or expired; the MCP server takes the token only in this header, not as access_token in the URL. Tools are missing, or the assistant calls a tool that no longer exists (Unknown tool) Clients keep the tool list from when the connection was made. After mapx changes its tools, disconnect the mapx connector in your client and connect it again (in claude.ai under Settings → Connectors), then start a new chat. Error page “Application not allowed” The application is not on the list of approved applications. Use the token way or write to support@mapx.at. 403 mcp-token-required A public (mx_pk_) or secret (mx_sk_) token was used at the MCP server. Create a token of type “AI assistant (MCP)”. 403 mcp-token-only An mx_mcp_ token was used for a direct API call. Use a secret token (mx_sk_) there. 429 A limit was exceeded. Wait the time stated in the message and make fewer calls in parallel. 403 for a browser client The Origin is not allowed. Browser clients must come from an allowed site; use a desktop client or the API.
data.with-a-token#With a token: Create a token at account.mapx.at/tokens/new?kind=mcp. Choose the type AI assistant (MCP), give it a name and optionally an expiry date. The token is shown once; copy it then. Add the server to your client (see below) and paste the token where the examples say YOUR_MCP_TOKEN. Ask a question that needs Austrian data. The token works only at the MCP server. It has no domain or IP binding, can have an expiry date, and you can block or rotate it at any time in your account.

data:
Routing runs on the Austrian road graph (GIP.at). Coordinates are lon,lat, joined with ;. Every request needs a token (Access and limits); the samples send it in the Authorization header, which browsers may send too.
Task Endpoint Zone Route between 2 to 25 points /v1/directions/{profile}/{coordinates} route Area reachable in N minutes /v1/isochrone/{profile}/{coordinate} heavy Travel times between many points /v1/matrix/{profile}/{coordinates} heavy Snap a GPS trace to roads /v1/matching/{profile}/{coordinates} heavy Best order of stops /v1/optimized-trips/{profile}/{coordinates} heavy Tours for several vehicles POST /v1/optimization heavy
data.a-route#A route: const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272?steps=true&language=en"; const { routes } = await (await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); const r = routes[0]; console.log(r.distance, "m", r.duration, "s"); overview=simplified (default) returns a light geometry, full every vertex, false none. steps=true adds turn-by-turn steps. alternatives=true adds up to two more routes[]. annotations=duration,distance,speed,maxspeed,elevation adds values per segment. With cycling_surface=any (default) unpaved sections are rated worse but stay allowed. Heights inside bridges and tunnels are not taken from the terrain model. maxspeed (step and annotation) is {speed, unit, legal}: legal: true marks a statutory limit (5, 10, 20 … 130 km/h), legal: false a modeled GIP speed such as 53 or 84 km/h, which is a routing speed and not a limit and must not be shown as a speed sign. {unknown: true} means no value (many motorways). Existing clients that only read speed and unit keep working. Cycling and walking steps carry grade_pct; the route summary has ascent, descent and elevation range.
data.closures#Closures:
driving, driving-traffic and driving-truck avoid every active full closure from the traffic reports (EVIS/ASFINAG), that is every report with closed: true in /v1/traffic/incidents. There are two kinds:
Kind Example Routing binding Binding closure (EVIS compliance option mandatory, traffic regulations) motorway ramp closed by order never driven true Full closure without that flag winter closure of a pass road, road closed for works driven only as a last resort, when start or destination lies on or behind the closure false routes[].closures_avoided lists the closures that the route without closures would have driven through (id, text, road, category, binding). If the route still runs through a closure because start or destination lies on or behind it, routes[].closures_unavoidable lists it; show it to the user as a warning. Time-conditional regulations (weekdays or hours only in the text) are only discouraged, by driving-traffic, and are not listed. Cycling and walking ignore the closures, the reports concern motor traffic. Source: ASFINAG, CC BY 4.0; show the texts unchanged.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/14.2,48.27;14.45,48.30?overview=false" | jq '.routes[0].closures_avoided'
data.handle-failures#Handle failures: 422 means the request is valid but unanswerable, for example no route between the points. 404 not-found: a start or destination is not on the road network (more than 1000 m away). 400 carries the faulty parameter in param. Retry 429 after Retry-After seconds. See Errors and limits.
data.isochrones-matrix-matching#Isochrones, m:
// Where can I walk in 5, 10 and 15 minutes? const iso = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/isochrone/walking/16.3725,48.2085?contours_minutes=5,10,15", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); // Travel times from the first point to the others const m = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/matrix/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272;14.2858,48.3069?sources=0&annotations=duration,distance", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); The isochrone result is a FeatureCollection of polygons, largest first. Each polygon carries contour and ready-made display values fill and fillOpacity; use contours_meters instead of contours_minutes for distance contours. Show it as a fill layer:
map.addSource("iso", { type: "geojson", data: iso }); map.addLayer({ id: "iso", type: "fill", source: "iso", paint: { "fill-color": ["get", "fill"], "fill-opacity": ["get", "fillOpacity"] } }); See Isochrone and Matrix. Map matching takes a GPS trace and returns the matched route.
data.next#Next: Directions API, Optimization API Traffic: incidents along a route Route example
data.offline-rerouting#Offline rerouting:
GET /v1/corridor-graph returns the road network around a route as one compact binary file (gzip stream, application/vnd.mapx.corridor-graph+gzip), so an app can recompute a route without network, for example after a wrong turn in a dead zone. Pass the route as polyline6 in polyline, the radius in buffer (100 to 5000 m, default 3000) and profile (driving default, cycling or walking). The file holds nodes, arcs with the travel times the router uses, road names, speed limits and turn restrictions; expect 1 to 3 MB per 100 km of route. Zone heavy. The endpoint needs a secret token (mx_sk_…); with a public token the API answers 403 pk-not-allowed. Source: GIP.at, CC BY 4.0.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -G "https://api.mapx.at/v1/corridor-graph" --data-urlencode "polyline@route.txt" -d buffer=500 -o corridor.mxcg
data.profiles#Profiles: Profile For driving Car driving-traffic Car, taking into account closures and traffic reports from ASFINAG and EVIS.AT (no network-wide traffic flow), lists reports in legs[].incidents driving-truck Trucks over 3.5 t cycling Bike: prefers cycle paths, lanes and signposted routes, rates unpaved sections and steep grades worse cycling-mtb Mountain bike: prefers forest tracks and singletrails, considers the MTB difficulty walking On foot Public transport is a separate API: Transit.
data.speed-limits-along-a-route#Speed limits:
GET /v1/speedlimits returns the statutory limits of the road network as compact GeoJSON, either in a box (bbox, at most 0.08 square degrees, about 28 by 28 km) or in a corridor around a route (corridor as polyline6 plus buffer in meters, default 30). Each road link is a LineString (digitizing direction) with limit_kmh, direction (both, forward, backward) and id. Links without a statutory limit are left out, so the sign display never shows a modeled speed.
# limits in a box curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/speedlimits?bbox=15.325,48.225,15.335,48.23" | jq '.features | length' # route as polyline6, then the limits in a 30 m corridor curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/15.6256,48.2049;15.3294,48.2272?geometries=polyline6&overview=full" | jq -j '.routes[0].geometry' > route.txt curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -G "https://api.mapx.at/v1/speedlimits" --data-urlencode "corridor@route.txt" -d buffer=30 | jq '.features | length' Write the polyline without a trailing newline (jq -j). Long routes can exceed the URL length of a GET request; split them into sections of about 500 points. Source: GIP.at, CC BY 4.0.
data.tolls#Tolls:
Car routes include toll_road, toll_road_m and toll with vignette products and special toll sections. toll_road and toll_road_m count only special toll sections (A9 Gleinalm/Bosruck, A10 Tauern/Katschberg, A11 Karawanken, A13 Brenner, S16 Arlberg); the vignette requirement is in toll.vignette_required and toll.vignette_m. toll.vignette_m counts the route meters on motorways and expressways of the road graph, without rest areas, special toll sections and the vignette-free sections of the ASFINAG data. Truck routes report the kilometers subject to the GO toll in routes[].toll.truck_go_km. Avoid tolls or motorways:
.../directions/driving/{coordinates}?exclude=toll .../directions/driving/{coordinates}?exclude=motorway,toll Vignette roads remain allowed with exclude=toll. Toll source: ASFINAG, CC BY 4.0.
exclude=motorway and exclude=toll work for driving, driving-traffic and driving-truck.
exclude=ferry closes all ferry links and works for every profile (driving, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb, walking) alone or combined, e.g. exclude=toll,ferry; driving-traffic returns 400. Because this variant is computed without contraction hierarchies, the response takes some tens of milliseconds longer. If a destination can only be reached by ferry (an island, for example), the request returns no route.
data.tour-planning#Tour planning:
optimized-trips orders up to 25 stops (round trip or fixed start and end). POST /v1/optimization plans tours for several vehicles with capacities and time windows. POST /v1/optimization needs a secret token (mx_sk_…) and belongs on a server; with a public token the API answers 403 pk-not-allowed.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -X POST https://api.mapx.at/v1/optimization -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "vehicles": [{ "id": 1, "start": [16.3725, 48.2083], "end": [16.3725, 48.2083] }], "services": [{ "id": 1, "location": [15.6256, 48.2049], "service": 300 }, { "id": 2, "location": [14.2858, 48.3069], "service": 300 }] }' | jq '.summary'
data.truck-routes#Truck routes: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving-truck/15.6256,48.2049;15.3294,48.2272?weight=40&height=4&width=2.55&length=16.5&truck_type=semi&overview=false" | jq '.routes[0] | {distance, duration, truck}' The router avoids roads closed to the vehicle: weight-class and trailer bans, height, width, weight and length limits. Speeds are capped at 80 km/h on motorways, 70 on rural roads, 50 in built-up areas. District-wide bans from free-text ordinances are not routed; affected roads are reported in steps[].notices[] with type: truck_restriction.
data.voice-and-banner-instructions#Voice and:
With steps=true you can add voice_instructions=true and banner_instructions=true (all road profiles: driving, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb and walking). The format follows Mapbox: each step carries the instructions for the maneuver at its end.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/15.6256,48.2049;15.3294,48.2272?steps=true&voice_instructions=true&banner_instructions=true&language=en&overview=false" | jq '.routes[0].legs[0].steps[1] | {voiceInstructions, bannerInstructions}' voiceInstructions[]: distanceAlongGeometry (meters before the end of the step at which to speak), announcement and ssmlAnnouncement. Announcement distances depend on speed: on motorways 2 km, 1 km and 300 m ahead, on rural roads 1 km, 400 m and 120 m, in town 400 m and 150 m; the last one is spoken without a distance. On foot the announcements come 100 m and 40 m ahead, by bike 250 m and 80 m ahead. The texts follow language (de or en) for every profile. The first step also announces the departure. bannerInstructions[]: primary and optional secondary with text, components[] (type icon for the road number, text for names and destination signage), type, modifier. With destination signage, the destination is the primary text and the road the secondary line.

data: Goal: a mapx map in an existing OpenLayers application (10.11.0), no build, with a free public token (see Access and limits).
data.add-the-basemap#Add the basemap:
The mapx styles are MapLibre styles with vector tiles. OpenLayers gets the same style rendered as raster tiles (Static Tiles): ol/source/XYZ with tile size 512. Styles: streets (and variants), light, dark, satellite, satellite-streets, outdoors, outdoors-winter; not available as raster tiles are traffic-day, traffic-night, satellite-current, the relief styles and the -3d styles.
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/ol@10.11.0/ol.css"> <script src="https://unpkg.com/ol@10.11.0/dist/ol.js">script> <div id="map" style="height:70vh">div> <script> const TOKEN = 'YOUR_TOKEN'; const map = new ol.Map({ target: 'map', layers: [new ol.layer.Tile({ source: new ol.source.XYZ({ url: 'https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets/tiles/512/{z}/{x}/{y}?access_token=' + TOKEN, tileSize: 512, maxZoom: 20, attributionsCollapsible: false, attributions: 'mapx.at, BEV, GIP.at, CC BY 4.0', }) })], view: new ol.View({ center: ol.proj.fromLonLat([16.37, 48.21]), zoom: 13 }), }); script> The token goes into the tile URL as access_token; API calls with fetch send it as the header Authorization: Bearer ….
data.attribution#Attribution: The data is licensed CC BY 4.0 and users must be able to reach the source on the map. Raster tiles have no TileJSON for OpenLayers to read the text from: set attributions yourself. attributionsCollapsible: false shows the text permanently; without it OpenLayers puts it behind an “i” button, like the MapLibre examples in these docs. The text per source is listed in Attribution and license.
data.examples#Examples: Examples with an OpenLayers version are listed in the overview (filter “OpenLayers”), for instance Embed a map and Route.
data.limits#Limits: No vector style: the basemap arrives as an image, labels and layers cannot be changed one by one. Use MapLibre for that. No 3D terrain and no 3D buildings, these are only available in MapLibre. Raster tiles count in the rate limit zone static (5 requests per second per IP address, briefly up to 60 at once, plus the per-minute limit of 6000 per token, see Access and limits). Ordinary panning and zooming stays well below that; only requesting new tiles faster for a sustained period returns 429.
data.your-own-geojson#Your own GeoJSON:
API responses (route, isochrone …) are GeoJSON in WGS84. ol.format.GeoJSON reads them into the map projection:
const source = new ol.source.Vector(); map.addLayer(new ol.layer.Vector({ source })); source.addFeatures(new ol.format.GeoJSON().readFeatures(geojson, { featureProjection: 'EPSG:3857' }));

data:
Goal: Place contour lines of suitable density over aerial imagery, draw index lines more strongly and label them with their elevation.
Prerequisites: a browser, a static web server and a free public token (Access and limits). Labels use the mapx fonts, see Style the basemap.
The contour lines tileset has a layer contour_l with the fields ele (elevation in m), index (1 = index line) and lvl (generalisation level 10, 12, 14, 16). Lines exist from z10.
Page with background. The orthophoto as base, the contours as a vector source:
<meta charset="utf-8"> <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.css"> <style>html, body, #map { margin: 0; height: 100%; }style> <div id="map">div> <script type="module"> import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs"; const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… // adds the token to every request to mapx.at (TileJSON, tiles, fonts) const withToken = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) && !url.includes("access_token=") ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url }); const sources = { ortho: { type: "raster", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/orthophoto.json", tileSize: 512 }, contours: { type: "vector", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/contours.json" } }; Draw the lines. Depending on the zoom the tileset delivers one level (lvl) with its own line interval:
Zoom lvl Interval Index line 10–11 10 100 m 500 m 12–13 12 50 m 200 m 14–15 14 20 m 100 m from 16 16 10 m 50 m Each tile holds only the level that matches its zoom, so the interval changes by itself and no filter on lvl is needed. Two layers are enough, lines and index lines:
const lineLayers = [ { id: "line", type: "line", source: "contours", "source-layer": "contour_l", filter: ["!=", ["get", "index"], 1], paint: { "line-color": "#ffd9a0", "line-width": 0.6, "line-opacity": 0.8 } }, { id: "index", type: "line", source: "contours", "source-layer": "contour_l", filter: ["==", ["get", "index"], 1], paint: { "line-color": "#ffb347", "line-width": 1.4 } } ]; Elevation labels. Only index lines carry a number. symbol-placement: "line" runs the text along the line:
const labels = { id: "ele-text", type: "symbol", source: "contours", "source-layer": "contour_l", minzoom: 12, filter: ["==", ["get", "index"], 1], layout: { "symbol-placement": "line", "text-field": ["concat", ["to-string", ["get", "ele"]], " m"], "text-font": ["Open Sans Semibold"], "text-size": 11 }, paint: { "text-color": "#fff", "text-halo-color": "#7a4a00", "text-halo-width": 1.5 } }; text-font must be a font that /v1/fonts lists (GET /v1/fonts), for example Open Sans Semibold or Noto Sans Regular. Without labels, drop this layer and glyphs.
Start the map.
const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, container: "map", transformRequest: withToken, center: [12.694, 47.074], zoom: 14, style: { version: 8, glyphs: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", sources: sources, layers: [{ id: "ortho", type: "raster", source: "ortho" }, ...lineLayers, labels] } }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once("load", () => map.getContainer().querySelector(".maplibregl-compact-show")?.classList.remove("maplibregl-compact-show")); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) </script>
data.next-steps#Next steps: Fields and levels in detail: Contour lines. Three-dimensional terrain: 3D terrain. Credits: Attribution.
data.result#Result:
Fine contour lines lie over the aerial imagery, their interval follows the zoom (100 m to 10 m). Index lines are strong and carry the elevation in metres.
For a map instead of imagery, replace the orthophoto layer with the layers from Style the basemap; put the contours on top.
Lines end below z10; for smaller scales the relief stays visible through hillshading.

data:
Goal: Use mapx orthophoto, elevation models and vector data as layers in QGIS, without a download. You need a free token (Access and limits); append ?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN to every layer URL. Use a secret token (mx_sk_…) on your own computer: a public token only works for its allowed origins, and QGIS is not a website.
Prerequisites: QGIS 3.x.
In QGIS you can load the tilesets (orthophoto, elevation models, vector tiles), but not the ready-made mapx styles: they read PMTiles files (pmtiles://). QGIS does not show the credit by itself; add it by hand in the print layout and in reports, see Attribution.
data.dtm-and-dsm#DTM and DSM:
The elevation tiles are Terrain-RGB: the elevation is stored in the colour channels. Use the same kind of connection with the URL
https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN (max. zoom 16; use dsm instead of terrain-rgb for the surface model). The layer first shows the encoded colour. Get the elevation in the Raster Calculator from the three bands:
-10000 + ("Layer@1" * 65536 + "Layer@2" * 256 + "Layer@3") * 0.1 (replace Layer with the name of your layer). The result is the elevation in metres; from it you can derive slope, aspect and hillshade.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Understand the elevation model: Terrain-RGB. Credits in maps and reports: Attribution.
data.orthophoto-as-an-xyz-layer#Orthophoto as:
In the Browser panel, right-click XYZ Tiles, New Connection.
Name mapx Orthophoto, URL:
https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/orthophoto/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN Min. Zoom Level 5, Max. Zoom Level 18, Tile Resolution 512 (Mapbox style, 512 px). Leave Referer and Authentication empty; the token in the URL is enough.
Save with OK and load the connection into the map by double-click.
The project CRS can be anything, QGIS reprojects the Web Mercator tiles.
data.vector-tiles#Vector tiles:
Browser panel, right-click Vector Tiles, New Generic Connection.
Name mapx Basemap, URL:
https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/streets/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN Enter Min. Zoom Level 0, Max. Zoom Level 16, OK.
Drag the connection into the map. QGIS first shows a default style; change the look in the layer style editor or with your own style.
The same procedure works for contours (max 16, min 10), orthophoto-flight-blocks (zoom 6 to 17). All tilesets: Tiles.

/guides/qgis/.title: mapx data in QGIS: XYZ and vector tiles

data:
Pick the endpoint by what the user does.
Task Endpoint Convert a typed address or place to coordinates /v1/geocode Show suggestions while the user types /v1/searchbox/suggest Fill a postal address form /v1/autofill/suggest Check an address /v1/address/validate Find the address at a point /v1/reverse Show places of a kind (fuel station, station) /v1/searchbox/category/{category} All data is official: the address register, place names, administrative boundaries from BEV. Requests are in the search zone, 10 per second and need a token (Access and limits); the samples send it in the Authorization header, which browsers may send too.
data.batch#Batch: POST /v1/geocode/batch geocodes up to 1000 queries in one request (zone heavy, 30 per minute). Batch geocoding needs a secret token (mx_sk_…) and therefore belongs on a server; with a public token the API answers 403 pk-not-allowed. An invalid item is returned as a problem object (status 400, code, param) at its position; the other items are answered.
data.geocode-an-address#Geocode an address:
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Herrengasse%2013,%201010%20Wien&types=address&limit=3"; const { features } = await (await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); const [lon, lat] = features[0].center; features can be empty; check the length before you read features[0]. Always pass types (address, street, locality, place, district, region, postcode, poi, road_ref for road kilometers such as A1 km 41). Narrow the result with bbox=minlon,minlat,maxlon,maxlat or rank by distance with proximity=lon,lat.
Postcode, place, street and house number come as separate fields in properties.address, no need to split place_name. A place after the house number takes precedence: Hauptplatz 12a Graz returns Graz (Hauptplatz 12, the street, the neighboring numbers), even if 12a exists only elsewhere. Coordinates such as 48.21, 16.37 as search text are answered like a reverse geocode.
data.next#Next: Geocoding API, Search Box API, Address API Errors and limits
data.places-by-category#Places by category: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/list/category?language=en" | jq ".listItems[0:3]" curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/category/gas_station?proximity=16.3725,48.2085&limit=5" list/category returns all category IDs with localized names (language=de or en).
data.type-ahead-search#Type-ahead search:
Call suggest on every pause in typing (debounce 200 ms), then retrieve once for the chosen entry. Send the same session_token for both calls.
const token = crypto.randomUUID(); const s = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/suggest?q=Stephansdom&proximity=16.3725,48.2085&limit=5&session_token=${token}`, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); const id = s.suggestions[0].mapbox_id; const r = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/searchbox/retrieve/${id}?session_token=${token}`, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); const [lon, lat] = r.features[0].geometry.coordinates; Suggestions carry a category (poi_category_ids, for example place_of_worship_church) and the administrative context. Cancel the previous request when a new key is typed (AbortController). Example: Search.

data: A static image is one HTTP request that returns a picture. Use it where an interactive map is not possible: PDFs, emails, listings, social previews. The token goes into the URL as access_token, because an image tag cannot send a header. For web pages use a public token (mx_pk_…) with your site as allowed origin; build images for e-mails and PDFs on your server with a secret token (mx_sk_…) so the secret does not end up in the message.
data.aerial-image-for-a-listing#Aerial image:
satellite shows the orthophoto, outdoors adds contours and trails.
https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/satellite/pin-m+ff0000(15.3294,48.2272)/15.3294,48.2272,17/800x600.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN Show the data credit next to the image, see Attribution.
data.fit-a-route-automatically#Fit a route au:
With auto instead of the view, the image shows all overlays.
const dir = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272?geometries=polyline&overview=simplified"; const { routes } = await (await fetch(dir, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); const path = encodeURIComponent(routes[0].geometry); // encoded polyline, precision 5 const url = `https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/outdoors/path-5+e11d48(${path})/auto/800x500@2x.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN`; The route comes from Directions with geometries=polyline.
data.next#Next: Static Images API Maps: the same styles interactively
data.overlays#Overlays:
Overlays come after the style, separated by commas (up to 50).
Overlay Example Pin pin-s+ff0000(16.3725,48.2085) (size s, m or l, color as hex) Path path-4+1d5bd8-0.8(encodedPolyline) (width, stroke, opacity; polyline precision 5, URL-encoded) GeoJSON geojson({...}) with simplestyle properties (URL-encoded) curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/static/streets/pin-s+ff0000(16.3725,48.2085)/16.3725,48.2085,14/600x400.png" -o vienna.png
data.raster-tiles-of-a-style#Raster tiles of: For clients that only read raster tiles (Leaflet, QGIS), Static Tiles render a style as 256 or 512 px tiles: /v1/styles/{id}/tiles/{256|512}/{z}/{x}/{y}.
data.url-format#URL format:
/v1/static/{style}/{view}/{width}x{height}[@2x][.png|.webp] /v1/static/{style}/{overlay}/{view}/{width}x{height}... Part Values style streets, streets-dawn, streets-dusk, streets-night, light, dark, satellite, satellite-streets, outdoors, outdoors-winter view lon,lat,zoom[,bearing] or auto (fits the overlays) size width and height 1 to 1280, up to 2560 with @2x format .png or .webp The relief styles (relief, relief-contours, relief-light, relief-dark) exist only for maps in the browser; as a static image the API answers 404. The same holds for the 3D styles (outdoors-3d, outdoors-winter-3d, relief-3d, satellite-3d, satellite-streets-3d, streets-3d, streets-night-3d, light-3d, dark-3d); for an image use the style without -3d. traffic-day and traffic-night show current traffic reports, which only the browser loads; as a static image they answer 404 with a hint to use streets or streets-night instead. satellite-current (Sentinel-2) is not available as an image either; use satellite. outdoors renders the full vector map as an image; buildings are drawn.
Images are in the heavy zone (30 per minute). They are cacheable: send If-None-Match and the API answers 304. Cache images on your side and do not request them per page view.

/guides/static-images/.title: Static images guide: map as image

data:
Goal: Build your own, consistently coloured map from the vector tiles of the basemap. mapx provides the data, you decide how it looks.
Prerequisites: a browser, a static web server and a free public token (Access and limits). Basic knowledge of MapLibre styles (sources and layers).
The basemap has 19 layers. This example uses five: landuse_a (land use), water_a (lakes), road_l (roads), building_a (buildings) and boundary_l (boundaries). All layers and fields are in the layer table.
Page and source. The source is the TileJSON link; zoom range and attribution come with it:
<meta charset="utf-8"> <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.css"> <style>html, body, #map { margin: 0; height: 100%; }style> <div id="map">div> <script type="module"> import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs"; const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… // adds the token to every request to mapx.at (TileJSON, tiles, fonts) const withToken = (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) && !url.includes("access_token=") ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url }); const source = { type: "vector", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/streets.json" }; Background and land use. Every polygon in landuse_a has a kind field (for example forest, farmland, vineyard, alpine_meadow, glacier, rock, residential). One colour per group via a match expression:
const landuse = { id: "landuse", type: "fill", source: "streets", "source-layer": "landuse_a", paint: { "fill-color": ["match", ["get", "kind"], "forest", "#bcd9b0", ["farmland", "vineyard"], "#efe9c8", "alpine_meadow", "#d9e8c4", "glacier", "#f4f8fb", "rock", "#d8d4cf", ["residential", "garden"], "#ebe5de", "#e6e9dc"] } }; Water. Lakes and ponds from water_a as polygons:
const water = { id: "water", type: "fill", source: "streets", "source-layer": "water_a", paint: { "fill-color": "#a9cde8" } }; Roads. road_l has kind: highway, major_road, minor_road, service, track, path. Let widths grow with zoom, draw paths thin and dashed:
const roads = { id: "roads", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "road_l", filter: ["in", ["get", "kind"], ["literal", ["highway", "major_road", "minor_road", "service"]]], layout: { "line-cap": "round", "line-join": "round" }, paint: { "line-color": ["match", ["get", "kind"], "highway", "#e8a35c", "major_road", "#f0c27a", "#ffffff"], "line-width": ["interpolate", ["exponential", 1.5], ["zoom"], 8, 0.5, 14, 3, 16, 8] } }; const trails = { id: "trails", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "road_l", minzoom: 13, filter: ["in", ["get", "kind"], ["literal", ["track", "path"]]], paint: { "line-color": "#a07a5a", "line-width": 1, "line-dasharray": [2, 1.5] } }; Buildings. building_a starts at z12 (merged there). From z15 each building has its own outline:
const buildings = { id: "buildings", type: "fill", source: "streets", "source-layer": "building_a", minzoom: 13, paint: { "fill-color": "#cfc7bd", "fill-outline-color": "#a89f94" } }; Boundaries. boundary_l carries kind (country, state, district, municipality). Strong lines for country and state, subtle for municipalities:
const boundaries = [ { id: "b-country", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "boundary_l", filter: ["==", ["get", "kind"], "country"], paint: { "line-color": "#7a4f8f", "line-width": 1.5 } }, { id: "b-state", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "boundary_l", filter: ["==", ["get", "kind"], "state"], paint: { "line-color": "#9d86a8", "line-width": 1, "line-dasharray": [4, 2] } }, { id: "b-municipality", type: "line", source: "streets", "source-layer": "boundary_l", minzoom: 10, filter: ["==", ["get", "kind"], "municipality"], paint: { "line-color": "#b9b0be", "line-width": 0.6, "line-dasharray": [2, 2] } } ]; Assemble the map. Order from bottom to top: land use, water, roads, buildings, boundaries.
const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, container: "map", transformRequest: withToken, center: [15.334, 48.227], zoom: 14, style: { version: 8, sources: { streets: source }, layers: [ { id: "ground", type: "background", paint: { "background-color": "#f2efe9" } }, landuse, water, roads, trails, buildings, ...boundaries ] } }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once("load", () => map.getContainer().querySelector(".maplibregl-compact-show")?.classList.remove("maplibregl-compact-show")); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) </script>
data.labels-and-fonts#Labels and fonts:
For labels (place_p, water_label_p, housenumber_p, road names from road_l via the field name) the style needs a glyphs entry. mapx serves fonts at /v1/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf (list: GET /v1/fonts, for example Open Sans Semibold, Noto Sans Regular). The withToken function from step 1 adds the token to these requests too:
style: { version: 8, glyphs: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf", sources: { streets: source }, layers: [ // ... { id: "places", type: "symbol", source: "streets", "source-layer": "place_p", filter: ["in", ["get", "kind"], ["literal", ["city", "town", "village"]]], layout: { "text-field": ["get", "name"], "text-font": ["Open Sans Semibold"], "text-size": 13 }, paint: { "text-color": "#333", "text-halo-color": "#fff", "text-halo-width": 1.5 } } ] } text-font must be a font that GET /v1/fonts lists.
data.next-steps#Next steps: All layers, fields and values: Basemap. Overlay contour lines and labels: Overlay contour lines. A map as an image for print: Static Images.
data.result#Result: A map in your own look: areas by land use, lakes, road network with trails, buildings and administrative boundaries. All data comes from a single tileset.
