data:
Traffic data covers the motorway and expressway network (ASFINAG, EVIS.AT) and planned roadworks on other roads. Requests are in the search zone, 10 per second, and need a token (Access and limits); the samples send it in the Authorization header, which browsers may send too.
Task Endpoint List incidents, roadworks and closures /v1/traffic/incidents Speed limits shown by variable message signs on motorways (no congestion data) /v1/traffic/sign-limits Positions of the signs /v1/traffic/signs Draw traffic on a map /v1/traffic/tiles.json Check whether the data is fresh /v1/traffic/status Route around closures profile driving-traffic (driving also avoids binding closures)
data.incidents-along-a-route#Incidents along:
Pass the route as route (encoded polyline, precision via route_precision 5 or 6, or a GeoJSON LineString). Results are sorted by position on the route. For long routes use POST with a JSON body.
# route Vienna–Graz as polyline6, then the reports in a 50 m corridor curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.4395,47.0707?geometries=polyline6" \ | jq '{route: .routes[0].geometry, route_precision: "6", type: "road_closure,construction", buffer: 50}' > body.json curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents --data @body.json | jq '.total' buffer is the corridor half-width in meters (1 to 1000, default 25).
data.lane-details-on-motorways#Lane details o:
Roadworks on motorways and expressways usually carry lanes from ASFINAG: one entry per direction and carriageway with the closed lanes (right, middle, left, hard_shoulder), the number of open lanes (open) out of original, contraflow, road_closed and the temporary speed_limit_kmh. direction is aligned (with increasing road kilometers) or opposite. sources lists where a report comes from (evis, asfinag); source names the dataset (evis-planned+asfinag when both match, asfinag-roadworks for roadworks only ASFINAG reports). The text of an EVIS report is never changed.
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?road=A12&type=construction"; const { features } = await (await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); for (const f of features) for (const l of f.properties.lanes ?? []) console.log(f.properties.road, l.closed, l.open, l.speed_limit_kmh);
data.list-incidents#List incidents:
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?bbox=16.0,48.0,16.8,48.5&type=road_closure,construction&limit=20"; const { features, total, next_cursor } = await (await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); for (const f of features) console.log(f.properties.road, f.properties.type, f.properties.text); Filters: bbox, road (A1, A 1 and A01 are the same road; ramps and branches such as road_section A13.33.4 belong to A13), road_class (motorway, expressway, federal, state, comma-separated, for A, S, B and L roads), type (accident, congestion, construction, lane_restriction, road_closure, road_hazard, miscellaneous), planned=true|false, and a time window with from and to (a date, or a date-time with Z or an offset such as 2026-12-01T10:00:00+01:00; to before from returns 400). By default only active reports are returned; active=false adds ended and future ones. A report with mandatory: true is binding; show its text unchanged.
Results are sorted by importance: closures and binding reports first, then motorways, expressways, federal and state roads, then by start. Page with limit (default 500, maximum 1000) and cursor: pass next_cursor from the response, or follow next, until next is null. With POST there is only next_cursor: send the same body again with cursor. total is the number of matches. Bad values for road, road_class, type or cursor return a 400 problem response.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?road=A1&road_class=motorway&limit=100" | jq '.total, .next' Every report has type and impact (critical closed for cars, major binding, lane restriction or accident, minor other unplanned, low other planned), kind (category of the source, in German, e.g. Straßensperre, Bauarbeiten), road (road number, null for municipal streets) and from EVIS road_name, direction (direction as text), regions (federal states), creator and transport_modes. closed: true means closed for cars; a road_closure with closed: false applies to other modes only (e.g. pedestrians, cycles) or traffic is led over the opposite carriageway.
data.next#Next: Traffic API Navigation: tolls, trucks, alternatives Attribution: credit ASFINAG and GIP.at
data.route-around-closures#Route around closu: GET /v1/directions/driving-traffic/{coordinates} The route avoids the current binding closures from the ASFINAG and EVIS.AT reports, discourages conditional closures and lists the reports along the way in legs[].incidents. Network-wide traffic flow (measured speeds, congestion on all roads) is not taken into account. Use incidents=true to get the list with other car profiles.
data.show-traffic-on-the-map#Show traffic on: map.on("load", () => { map.addSource("mx-traffic", { type: "vector", url: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/tiles.json" }); // layer "sign_limits": speed limits shown by variable message signs, per motorway section and direction map.addLayer({ id: "mx-sign-limits", type: "line", source: "mx-traffic", "source-layer": "sign_limits", paint: { "line-width": 4, "line-color": "#3a5fcd" } }); // layer "incidents": reports and closures (lines and points) map.addLayer({ id: "mx-incidents-lines", type: "line", source: "mx-traffic", "source-layer": "incidents", filter: ["!=", ["geometry-type"], "Point"], paint: { "line-width": 5, "line-color": "#b91c1c", "line-dasharray": [2, 1] } }); map.addLayer({ id: "mx-incidents-points", type: "circle", source: "mx-traffic", "source-layer": "incidents", filter: ["==", ["geometry-type"], "Point"], paint: { "circle-radius": 6, "circle-color": "#b91c1c", "circle-stroke-color": "#fff", "circle-stroke-width": 1.5 } }); }); The vector source has two layers: sign_limits (speed limits shown by variable message signs, with speed_limit, normal_speed and reduction in km/h; this is not a traffic state) and incidents (reports and closures with id, type, impact, start, end). The token is passed with transformRequest like on every map, see Access and limits. The mapx styles (for example streets) already use the source name traffic, so the source is called mx-traffic here. The styles traffic-day and traffic-night (night map with colors brightened for a dark background) draw both layers ready-made, the speed limits in a neutral color. Tiles are in the static zone (5 per second); let the client cache them.

data:
The timetable data covers Austria (ÖBB and the regional transport associations). It is the scheduled timetable: realtime is always false. Requests are in the route zone for journeys and the search zone for stops and departures. Every request needs a token (Access and limits); the samples send it in the Authorization header, which browsers may send too.
Task Endpoint Find stops near a point /v1/stops Next departures at a stop /v1/departures Journey from A to B /v1/directions/transit/{coordinates}
data.access-by-bike-or-car-bike--ride-park--r:
With access=bike or access=car the first leg is not walked but cycled or driven to a stop. Bikes can be locked at every stop (+2 min); cars park at stops with rail, metro or tram service (+3 min, at most 25 min drive); the algorithm takes the fastest combination, so the station in your own village wins over driving on to the next town if the train is quicker. Official P+R sites from the GIP are added for the car (+2 min, then a walk to the stop). Walking from the start still applies, the minimum counts. The exit is always on foot.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/isochrone/transit/15.16,48.207?contours_minutes=45&access=car" | jq '.metadata | {access, access_stops_improved, sites: .access_sites[:3]}' Parameter Values Meaning access foot (default), bike, car Mode to the first stop park any (default), official official: bike only at stops within 200 m of a B+R site, car only at official P+R sites sites 1 to 50 (default 10) Entries in metadata.access_sites metadata.access_sites lists the accesses that beat walking, sorted by travel time: source (site for an official P+R, stop for parking at the stop), kind, name, lon, lat, arrive_min (travel time), ready_min (ready to board, incl. parking and walk) and stops_won. Bringing the bike on the train (egress=bike) is not offered: the timetable data carry no bike-carriage information.
data.departure-board#Departure board:
Pass a stop id, or a coordinate to get the departures of all stops around it. A platform id such as at:43:7226:0:2 returns only the departures from that platform (stops[0] then carries platform_id and platform); the station id returns all platforms.
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/departures?stop=at:49:1320&limit=8"; const { departures } = await (await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); for (const d of departures) console.log(d.time.slice(11, 16), d.line.name, d.headsign, d.platform ?? ""); time is ISO 8601 in Vienna local time. Without time the request starts now. Use time (format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm, Vienna local time) for a later start and horizon (seconds, up to 24 hours) for the window. The timetable is valid for a limited period only: timetable.valid_from and timetable.valid_to in every response name it (around the December timetable change both timetable years are loaded together). Outside it the API answers 422, and the message (detail) names the valid period. Invalid dates or times such as 2026-02-31 or T25:00 answer 400. On the days the clocks change the times are exact; a local time that does not exist (between 02:00 and 03:00 in spring) moves on to summer time.
line.name is the line name passengers see, the same in departures and journeys: U1, S50, R52, bus numbers, long-distance trains by train number such as RJ 754. trip_short_name holds the train number.
data.find-stops#Find stops: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/stops?near=16.3725,48.2085&radius=300&limit=5" | jq '.stops[] | {id, name, modes, lines}' Stops of the same station from different operators are merged and share one id (for example at:49:1320). Use bbox (at most one square degree) to list a map section.
data.journey-planning#Journey planning: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/transit/16.3725,48.2085;16.4202,48.1855" | jq '.routes[0].duration' Pass exactly an origin and a destination. Use depart_at (earliest departure) or arrive_by (latest arrival), each in the format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm in Vienna local time; the default is now. The response contains several journeys in routes[] (the number can be set with routes, see the transit API), with walking sections on the road network and rides with line, stops, times and platform (from.platform, to.platform, stops[].platform, null if unknown). Changing at the same station takes at least 2 minutes, after a walk at least 1 minute remains before the departure. With bike_transit the first leg is cycled; the bike stays at the stop, changes and the last leg are walked. No stop within reach or no connection: 422.
data.next#Next: Transit API Navigation Attribution: timetable data credit
data.reachability-by-transit#Reachability by:
Walking plus public transport as isochrones: profile transit of the isochrone API. The search walks to the stops around the start, rides the scheduled timetable from depart_at and walks on from every stop reached.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/isochrone/transit/16.3725,48.2085?contours_minutes=10,20,30" | jq '.features[] | {contour: .properties.contour, km2: .properties.area_km2}' Without depart_at the isochrone starts now (Vienna local time); use depart_at to pick another time. Only contours_minutes applies. The area depends strongly on the time: the same start has a much smaller area at night. Outside the timetable period the API answers 422.
data.show-departures-in-an-app#Show departure: Search a stop with /v1/stops or let the user click the map. Call /v1/departures and refresh every minute. Show line, destination and time; label the times as “scheduled” (timetable data).

data: The official data in mapx is licensed under CC BY 4.0. The Sentinel-2 tiles are the exception: they contain modified Copernicus Sentinel data and follow the Copernicus terms; the credit is in the TileJSON. You may use it commercially. You must name the source and the license and must not present modifications as official. Users must be able to reach the credit on the map itself, for example as text in the corner or behind an “i” info button on the map, not only in an imprint.
data.in-a-maplibre-map#In a MapLibre map:
MapLibre shows the attribution automatically when you load a style or a TileJSON (bottom right). The examples in these docs collapse it so it does not cover the map: attributionControl: false in the map options and map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })) show an “i” button, a click shows the sources. MapLibre first shows the compact form open and collapses it on the first map drag; the map.once("load", …) line from the examples collapses it right after loading. attributionControl: false without your own AttributionControl hides the sources completely, which is not allowed. If you use tiles: [...] without TileJSON, add the text to the source yourself:
{ type: "raster", tiles: ["https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/orthophoto/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"], tileSize: 512, maxzoom: 18, attribution: "mapx.at; Orthophoto: BEV, CC BY 4.0" }
data.in-print-reports-and-static-images#In pr: Put a visible line next to the image, in readable size, for example Source: mapx.at; BEV – ALS-DTM 1 m (2025-09-15), CC BY 4.0. With several sources list them all, separated by semicolons.
data.mapxat-first#mapx.at first: Every mapx attribution starts with mapx.at, followed by the data sources. The styles under /v1/styles carry mapx.at with a link to https://mapx.at as their first entry (own source mapx with the layer mapx-attribution); please do not remove it. If you add tilesets directly you get the link through the TileJSON (attribution starts with mapx.at), the JSON responses of the API through their attribution field (mapx.at; …). MapLibre orders the entries by length, shortest first: your own sources with a very short attribution (under 68 characters) appear before it. With Leaflet, OpenLayers and static images put mapx.at in front yourself, as in the examples.
data.text-per-api#Text per API:
JSON responses with data carry a top-level attribution field; it always starts with mapx.at; before the source from the table. Show it when you display or pass on the data.
API Source Geocoding, Search Box, Address BEV (address register, geographical names, administrative boundaries), CC BY 4.0 Directions, Isochrone, Matrix, Matching GIP.at, CC BY 4.0 Tolls, Traffic ASFINAG / EVIS.AT, CC BY 4.0, road network GIP.at Public transport ÖBB-Personenverkehr AG (CC BY 4.0), data source Mobilitätsverbünde Österreich OG Weather GeoSphere Austria, CC BY 4.0 Climate GeoSphere Austria (APOLIS, SPARTACUS, SNOWGRID-CL, WINFORE), CC BY 4.0 Air quality GeoSphere Austria (chemical weather model), CC BY 4.0 Tilequery Source of the queried tileset, see Tilesets Elevation BEV – ALS-DTM / ALS-DOM 1 m, CC BY 4.0 The credit is also stored in the TileJSON.
data.text-per-tileset#Text per tileset: Tileset Text streets mapx.at; Datenquellen: BEV (DKM, Verwaltungsgrenzen, Adressregister, Geographische Namen), GIP.at, BMLUK (GGN), Umweltbundesamt, Stadt Wien – data.wien.gv.at; CC BY 4.0 contours mapx.at; Höhenlinien: mapx.at, Datenquelle BEV – ALS-DTM 1 m (Stichtag 15.09.2025), CC BY 4.0 terrain-rgb mapx.at; Relief: BEV – ALS-DTM 1 m (Stichtag 15.09.2025), CC BY 4.0 dsm mapx.at; Relief: BEV – ALS-DOM 1 m (Stichtag 15.09.2025), CC BY 4.0 orthophoto mapx.at; Orthophoto: BEV (CC BY 4.0) orthophoto-flight-blocks The TileJSON only names mapx.at; credit mapx.at; BEV, CC BY 4.0, since the flight blocks are metadata of the BEV orthophoto. bike-routes mapx.at; Datenquelle: GIP.at, CC BY 4.0 gip-poi mapx.at; Datenquelle: GIP.at, CC BY 4.0 rest-areas mapx.at; ASFINAG, CC BY 4.0 sharing mapx.at; ÖBB-Personenverkehr AG – Shared-Mobility Standorte, CC BY 4.0 sentinel2, sentinel2-date, sentinel2-ndvi, sentinel2-ndwi, sentinel2-ndsi mapx.at; Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026 (year of the images; stated in the TileJSON)

data.epsg4326-and-epsg3857#EPSG:4326 and EPSG:
EPSG:4326 (WGS84) EPSG:3857 (Web Mercator) Unit degrees metres Used for input and output of the APIs, GeoJSON, GPS tile scheme of maps Example 12.694, 47.074 1413090, 5954161 Inputs to the APIs are always WGS84 (EPSG:4326). Tiles are in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), see Tile scheme. Clients convert between them themselves; you do not need to compute tile coordinates.
Web Mercator distances in Austria are about 50 % larger than true metres (factor 1 / cos(latitude)). Do not measure lengths and areas in EPSG:3857; use geodesic measurement or a local system such as EPSG:31287 (MGI / Austria Lambert) or EPSG:3035 (ETRS89-LAEA).
data.official-sources-mgi-and-etrs89#Official:
The authorities’ source data uses different systems: Austrian national survey (MGI, for example Gauss-Krüger M28/M31/M34 and Lambert) and ETRS89 (for example ETRS89-LAEA, UTM). Between MGI and WGS84/ETRS89 there is a positional offset of several metres that is corrected with an official transformation grid.
mapx transforms correctly: all products are converted to WGS84 and Web Mercator with the official transformation procedure. You get layers that line up without applying a transformation yourself. When you overlay your own official data in MGI, use the transformation grid of your software (for example QGIS with the BEV grid), otherwise it shifts by a few metres.
data.order-longitude-first#Order: longitude f:
All mapx interfaces, TileJSON, MapLibre and GeoJSON use lon, lat (longitude, then latitude), that is east-west before north-south:
12.694,47.074 // lon,lat: Großglockner area Many map apps and GPS devices show lat, lon instead. Swapped values end up in the Indian Ocean, not in Austria. The elevation API expects points=lon,lat;lon,lat. Leaflet takes [lat, lon] in L.latLng, MapLibre and OpenLayers [lon, lat].

data.aerialway_l#aerialway_l:
Geometry: LineZoom: z12–16Layer: aerialway_l
Cable cars and lifts (lines).
Field Type Description kind string Type of installation. Possible values Meaning cable_car Aerial tramway gondola Gondola lift chair_lift Chair lift drag_lift Drag lift goods Goods cableway (incl. avalanche-control cableway) inclined_lift Inclined lift zip_line Zip line min_zoom number Zoom level from which the feature is shown. name string Name of the feature.
data.airport_p#airport_p:
Geometry: PointZoom: z8–16Layer: airport_p
Airports, airfields and heliports.
Field Type Description icao string ICAO code (4 letters), if available. kind string Type of aerodrome. Possible values Meaning airport Commercial airport airfield Airfield heliport Heliport military Military airfield min_zoom number Zoom level from which the feature is shown. name string Name of the feature.
data.boundary_l#boundary_l:
Geometry: LineZoom: z0–16Layer: boundary_l
Administrative boundaries (lines).
Field Type Description admin_level number Administrative level of the boundary (2 country, 4 state, 6 district, 8 municipality). Possible values Meaning 2 Country border 4 State border 6 District border 8 Municipality border kind string Type of boundary. Possible values Meaning country Country state State district District municipality Municipality left string Name of the administrative unit on the left of the line (not set for country borders). min_zoom number Zoom level from which the feature is shown. right string Name of the administrative unit on the right of the line (for country borders the adjoining area).
data.boundary_label_p#boundary_label_p:
Geometry: PointZoom: z4–16Layer: boundary_label_p
Label points for states, districts and municipalities.
Field Type Description admin_level number Administrative level. Possible values Meaning 4 State 6 District 8 Municipality code string Official code of the unit. kind string Type of administrative unit. Possible values Meaning state State district District municipality Municipality min_zoom number Zoom level from which the feature is shown. name string Name of the feature.
data.building_a#building_a:
Geometry: PolygonZoom: z12–16Layer: building_a
Building footprints.
Field Type Description has_parts boolean true when the building's body is in building_part_a (Vienna, from z15); 3D displays then extrude only the parts. height number Building height in metres above ground. From the BEV building model (DLM structures); where it has none, from the elevation models (surface model minus terrain model, median within the footprint). At z12 to z14 (merged buildings) the area-weighted mean of the buildings in the area, in whole metres. kind string Building type; ordinary buildings are plain, notable buildings are marked separately. Possible values Meaning building Building (general) church Church chapel Chapel castle Castle, palace fire_station Fire station hospital Hospital pharmacy Pharmacy police Police power Power plant, substation school School station Station building townhall Town hall or district office hut Mountain hut max_height number Maximum height of the building in metres (towers, churches), only when clearly above the building height; from z15. min_zoom number Zoom level from which the feature is shown.
data.building_part_a#building_part_a:
Geometry: PolygonZoom: z13–16Layer: building_part_a
Building parts with bottom and top for 3D display (extrude from min_height to height): tower parts of tall buildings derived from the surface model (from z13), in Vienna the blocks of the City of Vienna building block model (from z15, replacing the whole body there, see building_a.has_parts).
Field Type Description height number Top of the part in metres above ground. min_height number Bottom of the part in metres above ground (tower part: building height or top of the part below; Vienna: 0, or the underside for passages and canopies). source string Origin of the part. Possible values Meaning dsm derived from the surface model (BEV ALS) wien City of Vienna building block model
data.housenumber_p#housenumber_p:
Geometry: PointZoom: z16–16Layer: housenumber_p
House numbers.
Field Type Description housenumber string House number. kind string Object the number refers to. Possible values Meaning building Building parcel Parcel street string Street name.
data.landuse_a#landuse_a:
Geometry: PolygonZoom: z2–16Layer: landuse_a
Land use and land cover (polygons).

data: Terrain-RGB stores one elevation per pixel in the three color channels of an image. This lets elevation tiles be served in ordinary image formats, and clients such as MapLibre compute shading and 3D terrain from them.
data.decoding#Decoding: const hoehe = (r, g, b) => -10000 + (r * 65536 + g * 256 + b) * 0.1; hoehe = -10000 + (r.astype("uint32") * 65536 + g * 256 + b) * 0.1 # r, g, b als numpy-Arrays
data.formula#Formula: height_m = -10000 + (R · 65536 + G · 256 + B) · 0.1 R is the most significant byte. The value q = R·65536 + G·256 + B lies between 0 and 16,777,215, so the elevation lies between −10,000 m and +1,667,721.5 m in steps of 0.1 m.
data.what-to-watch-for#What to watch for: Read the image format losslessly. mapx serves lossless WebP. Any lossy intermediate step (JPEG, color profile, premultiplied alpha, scaling while decoding) distorts the elevation. Do not interpolate before decoding. Blending RGB values does not give a blended elevation. Decode first, then average. Mapbox-compatible. encoding: "mapbox" in MapLibre. Terrarium (R·256 + G + B/256 − 32768) is a different encoding and is not served by mapx. 512 pixels, no border. tileSize: 512. Application: DTM terrain model.

data: All mapx tiles follow the common web map scheme. With MapLibre, Leaflet, OpenLayers or QGIS you do not need to configure anything; for your own requests and calculations, here is what matters.
data.512-pixel-tiles#512-pixel tiles:
mapx raster tiles (elevation models, orthophoto) are 512 × 512 pixels, not 256. A 512 tile covers the same area as four 256 tiles one level deeper. Clients need the right setting:
MapLibre: tileSize: 512 (automatic with TileJSON). Leaflet: tileSize: 512, zoomOffset: -1. OpenLayers: tileSize: 512 on the source. QGIS: tile resolution 512. If you forget it, the map looks off by one zoom level and blurry or too fine.
data.further-reading#Further reading: Elevation values in tiles: Terrain-RGB. Coordinates and projections: Coordinates.
data.overzoom#Overzoom:
If a level is higher than the stored one, the client scales up the tiles of the highest level (overzoom). The image does not get sharper, but the map stays usable. In MapLibre set maxzoom of the source to the highest existing level (automatic from TileJSON); the map itself may zoom further. Requests outside the zoom range return 404, tiles inside the zoom range but outside Austria return 204 with no content, see Errors and limits. Requests outside the zoom range return 404; tiles inside the zoom range but outside Austria return 204 with no content, see Errors and limits.
Vector tiles are not redrawn on overzoom; the geometry of the highest level is stretched.
data.projection-and-address#Projection and ad:
The world is projected in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) onto a square and divided into zoom levels. At level z the square has 2^z × 2^z tiles. A tile is addressed as z/x/y: x counts from west to east, y from north to south (XYZ scheme, not TMS), both starting at 0.
Tile for a point lon, lat (degrees) at level z:
function tile(lon, lat, z) { const n = 2 ** z; const x = Math.floor(((lon + 180) / 360) * n); const r = (lat * Math.PI) / 180; const y = Math.floor(((1 - Math.log(Math.tan(r) + 1 / Math.cos(r)) / Math.PI) / 2) * n); return { z, x, y }; } tile(12.694, 47.074, 12); // { z: 12, x: 2192, y: 1439 } A tile is served by https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/{tileset}/{z}/{x}/{y}.{ext}, see Tiles.
data.resolution-per-zoom-level#Resolution per:
Resolution depends on latitude. The table applies to 47.5° N, the middle of Austria:
Zoom m per pixel Tile edge (km) Note z5 1,652 846 z6 826 423 z7 413 212 z8 207 106 z9 103 53 z10 52 26 z11 26 13 z12 13 6.61 z13 6.46 3.30 z14 3.23 1.65 z15 1.61 0.83 z16 0.81 0.41 highest stored level (≈ 1 m source) z17 0.40 0.21 overzoom (client) One level deeper halves the pixel size. The elevation models exist up to z16, the orthophoto up to z18.

mapx needs a free account and an API token (get one in a minute). Pick a page and copy the code. Code samples use YOUR_TOKEN as a placeholder.
What is mapx The products in one minute. Access and limits Free token, rate limits, attribution. First map in 5 minutes One HTML file. First search Find an address with one request. First route Drive from Vienna to Melk. Glossary Tile, TileJSON, profile, isochrone and more. FAQ Short answers to common questions.
data.next#Next: Guides: one guide per product. Reference: every endpoint with a playground.

data.attribution#Attribution: Show the source of the data wherever the map or result is visible. MapLibre adds the text for you when you load a style or TileJSON. See Attribution.
data.cors-and-caching#CORS and caching:
CORS allows every origin, so you can call the APIs straight from the browser. The preflight answer allows the Authorization header, so fetch calls from the browser can send the token in the header; image and tile URLs take it as access_token. If a request carries both a Bearer token and access_token, the Bearer token counts; another Authorization scheme (for example Basic of a proxy) does not hide access_token.
All responses to requests with a token are Cache-Control: private: the browser may cache them, shared caches (proxies, CDNs) must not, so no one else gets your response without a token. Every GET response carries an ETag; send it back as If-None-Match and you get 304 Not Modified without a body (tiles, styles and TileJSON use the file version, all other responses the content, for example traffic reports polled every minute).
data.get-a-token#Get a token:
All endpoints under https://api.mapx.at/v1/ and all tiles under https://tiles.mapx.at/ need a token. It is free.
Open account.mapx.at and sign in with your e-mail address (an 8-digit code is sent to you) or with Google or Microsoft. If there is no account for the address yet, you create it after entering the code with “Create account”; you tick the box for the terms of use, the privacy policy and contact about the service and your account (security, changes, shutdown). The newsletter is optional, there or later in your account. Code emails are limited per address and per connection; if you see “Too many attempts”, try again a little later. Under Tokens use New token to create a named token (up to 100 per account). The token is shown once; copy it then. Send the token with every request (see below).
data.kinds-of-token#Kinds of token: Kind Prefix Use Restrictions Public mx_pk_… Websites and apps. The token is visible in the page source or in the APK, so it only works where you allow it. Read-only products, GET/HEAD only. Not for POST /v1/optimization, POST /v1/geocode/batch and /v1/corridor-graph (otherwise 403 pk-not-allowed). Bound to allowed origins (for example https://example.com, *.example.com) or to an Android app (package name plus SHA-256 of the signing certificate). Secret mx_sk_… Servers, scripts and CI. Never put it into a web page or an app. No origin binding; optionally bound to IP ranges (CIDR). AI assistant (MCP) mx_mcp_… AI assistants and agents that use the mapx MCP server. Created by hand or by signing in with your account (then shown as “connected via ”). Works only at https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp, no origin or IP binding, optional expiry date. Direct API calls with it answer 403 mcp-token-only. A public token is checked against the Origin header (for tiles and images without one, against the Referer host). Requests from other sites get 403 with the reason origin-not-allowed. An origin is scheme, host and port, for example http://localhost:3000 while you develop; add localhost only during development. A page opened as a file (file://) has no origin: use a local web server (npx serve).
data.managing-tokens-and-your-account#Managin: Edit: You can change the name, allowed origins or Android app, IP ranges and expiry date later; changes take effect immediately. Wildcards need your own domain after them (*.example.com, not *.at), and an IP range /0 is not allowed (leave the field empty instead). Expiry date: given in UTC. Once set, an expiry date can only be brought forward, not extended. Rotate: creates a new token with the same settings; the old one keeps working for 7 days so you can replace it calmly. Block: the token is rejected immediately (token-blocked) and can be unblocked again. Delete takes effect immediately and permanently. Usage: the Overview and Usage pages show requests per token, product and day, rejected ones with the reason (e.g. origin-not-allowed). “Last used” is updated about once a minute. Account: under Account you can change your address (shortly after signing in; a code is sent to the new address), turn the newsletter on or off, export all your data as JSON and delete the account. Deleting the account deletes all tokens; applications using them stop working immediately. The OpenAPI description https://api.mapx.at/v1/openapi.json and CORS preflight requests (OPTIONS) work without a token.
data.next#Next: First map in 5 minutes Errors and limits
data.no-warranty#No warranty: All mapx data and results are provided without guarantee and used at your own risk. Check results yourself, especially for addresses, routes, departures, weather. The terms of use apply.
data.rate-limits#Rate limits:
The zones below apply per IP address (per token over MCP). On top of that, each token may make 6000 requests per minute by default; rejected requests with rate-limited are counted too. Every API response carries a RateLimit-Policy header, for example "search";q=10;w=1;burst=30 (10 requests per second plus a burst of 30); the gateway sets it from the same table as its limits, so it always names the zone that actually applies. The PMTiles requests of the styles (https://tiles.mapx.at/…pmtiles) do not carry it; they count in the tiles zone. Exceeding a limit returns 429 with Retry-After. A daily and a monthly limit per account are also planned (all tokens together, UTC; when exceeded: 429 quota-exceeded with Retry-After until the next day or month); currently both are unlimited. Your account shows the current state under Usage.
Zone Requests Used by tiles 100/s, burst 200 tiles, TileJSON, glyphs and sprites (burst 100), PMTiles requests of the styles (burst 500 on tiles.mapx.at) search 10/s, burst 30 styles and the lists /v1/styles, /v1/tiles, geocoding, Search Box, autofill, address validation, tilequery, departures, stops, weather values, traffic reports route 5/s, burst 20 directions, transit journeys, speed limits (corridor graph: burst 10) elevation 10/s, burst 20 elevation and profile static 5/s, burst 60 Static Tiles, traffic tiles weather 20/s, burst 200 weather tiles (a radar animation loads 70 to 150 tiles at once) heavy 30/min, burst 5 static images, isochrone, matrix, matching, optimized trips, optimization (burst 3) batch 2/min, burst 2 batch geocoding (up to 1000 addresses per request, one request at a time) Expensive groups (rendered tiles and static images, routing, search, batch geocoding) also have an overall limit for all clients together, so that a single client cannot use up the server. It answers 429 with Retry-After as well.
Over MCP. Every tool call of the MCP server counts like an API call (some tools make several) and shows up as MCP in the usage view. The per-minute limit of the token and the zone limits above apply, per token instead of per IP address. The MCP endpoint itself accepts 10 requests per second per IP address (burst 40) and request bodies up to 256 KB.
For many tiles: cache responses in the client (tiles change only with a new release) and on 429 retry after Retry-After. Details and retry advice: Errors and limits.
data.send-the-token#Send the token:
Use the header in server code and scripts. In the browser fetch calls can send the header as well; use the query parameter where no header can be set, for example in image URLs and MapLibre tile URLs.
# header curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Melk&limit=1" | jq # query parameter curl -s "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Melk&limit=1&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN" | jq const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Melk&access_token=YOUR_TOKEN"); // the query parameter works everywhere; the header works in the browser too Maps with MapLibre GL JS. The simplest way is a transformRequest that adds the token to every request to mapx.at, never to other hosts:
const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… // the mapx styles load their tiles from PMTiles files: register the protocol once maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, container: "map", style: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets", center: [16.3725, 48.2085], zoom: 13, // Vienna, lon,lat transformRequest: (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) && !url.includes("access_token=") ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url, }), }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once("load", () => map.getContainer().querySelector(".maplibregl-compact-show")?.classList.remove("maplibregl-compact-show")); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) PMTiles prerequisite. The mapx styles load their tiles from PMTiles files. The page must therefore include pmtiles.js () and call maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new pmtiles.Protocol().tile) once; otherwise the map stays empty (console: URL scheme "pmtiles" is not supported). Your own styles that only use TileJSON sources (https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/{tileset}.json) do not need it.
When you request a style with ?access_token=…, the API writes the token into all mapx.at URLs of the style (tiles, glyphs, sprites, PMTiles files). That is why the transformRequest above adds the token only when access_token is not in the URL yet. Clients that cannot set transformRequest work with style: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN" (they still need the PMTiles protocol). Such a response is private and must not be shared.
Android. Send Authorization: Bearer plus X-Mapx-Android-Package (package name) and X-Mapx-Android-Cert (SHA-256 of the signing certificate, read at run time with PackageManager).
Without a valid token the API answers 401 (missing-token, invalid-token, token-expired) or 403 (token-blocked, pk-not-allowed, origin-missing, origin-not-allowed, app-not-allowed, ip-not-allowed) as application/problem+json; see Errors and limits.

data.can-i-download-the-tiles#Can I download: No. mapx delivers maps and tiles through the API: style, TileJSON or {z}/{x}/{y}, see Maps and QGIS. Whole tileset files for self-hosting are not offered.
data.can-i-use-mapx-with-claude-chatgpt-or-cu: Yes, through the MCP server: 21 read-only tools for Austrian data. In claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code you only enter https://mcp.mapx.at/mcp and sign in with your mapx account. For Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI and other clients, create a token of type “AI assistant (MCP)”.
data.do-i-need-a-token-or-an-account#Do I nee: Yes, a free account and API token. Sign in at account.mapx.at with your email address (the first time, this creates the account), create a token and send it as Authorization: Bearer or access_token. CORS is open. See Access and limits.
data.does-a-url-change-when-there-is-new-data: API URLs (/v1/tiles/streets/..., TileJSON) stay the same. Styles and TileJSON always point to the current data.
data.how-current-is-the-data#How current is t: Each tileset has a source date, shown on its page under Tilesets and in the stand field of GET /v1/tiles.
data.is-mapx-free#Is mapx free?: Yes, with an account and a token. The rate limits apply per IP address and zone, plus a per-minute limit per token, see Access and limits.
data.is-there-data-outside-austria#Is there d: Austria only. Orthophoto and base map reach a little into neighboring countries at the border.
data.may-i-use-it-commercially#May I use it c: Yes. The official data is licensed CC BY 4.0: name the source. The Sentinel-2 tiles follow the Copernicus terms; details are under Sources and licenses and in the terms of use.
data.my-map-is-blurry#My map is blurry: Raster tiles are 512 px. Set tileSize: 512 in your client. See Tile scheme.
data.my-points-land-in-the-wrong-country#My p: Longitude and latitude are swapped. mapx and GeoJSON use lon,lat. See Coordinates.
data.what-is-the-difference-between-dtm-and-d: The DTM is bare ground, the DSM includes trees and buildings. Use the DTM for gradients and profiles, the DSM for visibility and building heights. See Elevation.
data.where-do-i-report-a-problem#Where do I r: Write to support@mapx.at (technical questions and bugs) or info@mapx.at (everything else).
data.why-do-i-get-401-or-403#Why do I get 401: 401 means the token is missing, invalid or expired. 403 means it is blocked, or a public token is used from an origin or app that is not allowed (origin-not-allowed), or a public token calls an endpoint that needs a secret token (pk-not-allowed). The code in the error body (and the X-Mapx-Reason header) names the reason. See Access and limits and error codes.
data.why-do-i-get-404-for-a-tile#Why do I get: The zoom is outside the range of the tileset, the extension does not match the type (pbf vector, webp raster), or the tileset name is wrong. Tiles inside the zoom range but outside Austria return 204 with no content.
data.why-do-i-get-429#Why do I get 429?: You exceeded the rate limit of the zone. Wait Retry-After seconds and retry with growing delay. For heavy loads, cache tiles in the client.

data:
Save the code as index.html, run npx serve in the folder and open the printed address (http://localhost:3000). Replace YOUR_TOKEN with a public token from account.mapx.at and add http://localhost:3000 as an allowed origin for the token. Double-clicking the file is not enough: without a web server there is no origin and the API answers 403. No build step.
<html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8"> <title>First mapx maptitle> <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.css"> <script src="https://unpkg.com/pmtiles@4.5.0/dist/pmtiles.js">script> <style>html, body, #map { margin: 0; height: 100%; }style> head> <body> <div id="map">div> <script type="module"> import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6.19.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs"; const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // public token mx_pk_… // the style loads PMTiles files: register the pmtiles:// protocol once maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, container: "map", style: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets", // adds the token to every request to mapx.at (style, tiles, fonts, sprites) transformRequest: (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) && !url.includes("access_token=") ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url }), center: [16.3725, 48.2085], // Vienna, lon,lat zoom: 13, }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once("load", () => map.getContainer().querySelector(".maplibregl-compact-show")?.classList.remove("maplibregl-compact-show")); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) script> body> html> Prerequisite: the mapx styles load their tiles from PMTiles files. The page must therefore include pmtiles.js and call maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new pmtiles.Protocol().tile) once; otherwise the map stays empty (console: URL scheme "pmtiles" is not supported). Your own styles that only use TileJSON sources (https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/{tileset}.json) do not need it.
The style streets is a normal MapLibre style. Replace it with satellite or outdoors to change the look. All styles: Styles API.
MapLibre GL JS 6.19.0 is the version these examples are tested with.

data.draw-it-on-the-map#Draw it on the map:
With the map from First map in map:
const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272?overview=simplified"; const route = (await (await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json()).routes[0]; const draw = () => { map.addSource("route", { type: "geojson", data: { type: "Feature", geometry: route.geometry } }); map.addLayer({ id: "route", type: "line", source: "route", paint: { "line-color": "#1d5bd8", "line-width": 5 } }); const bounds = new maplibregl.LngLatBounds(); route.geometry.coordinates.forEach((c) => bounds.extend(c)); map.fitBounds(bounds, { padding: 40 }); }; map.loaded() ? draw() : map.once("load", draw); // the map may already be loaded when the route arrives

data.request#Request:
Coordinates are always lon,lat, separated by ;.
curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272?overview=false" \ | jq '.routes[0] | {distance, duration}' const url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272?overview=simplified"; const { routes } = await (await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); console.log(routes[0].distance / 1000, "km", routes[0].duration / 60, "min"); import requests url = "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving/16.3725,48.2085;15.3294,48.2272" route = requests.get(url, params={"overview": "simplified"}, headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}).json()["routes"][0] print(route["distance"] / 1000, "km", route["duration"] / 60, "min") The response of the curl example looks like this: {"distance":90076.3,"duration":3649.0}. distance is in meters, duration in seconds. On 401 or 403 see Access and limits. Other profiles: driving-traffic (avoids reported closures), driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb and walking; parameters per profile in the Directions reference. See the Navigation guide.

data.request#Request: curlJavaScriptPython curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Stephansplatz%201,%20Wien&types=address&limit=1" | jq '.features[0] | {place_name, center}' const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode?q=Stephansplatz%201,%20Wien&types=address&limit=1", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }); const { features } = await res.json(); console.log(features[0].place_name, features[0].center); // center is [lon, lat] import requests res = requests.get("https://api.mapx.at/v1/geocode", params={"q": "Stephansplatz 1, Wien", "types": "address", "limit": 1}, headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}) feature = res.json()["features"][0] print(feature["place_name"], feature["center"]) The response is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection; the curl example returns, for example, {"place_name":"Stephansplatz 1, Innere Stadt, 1010 Wien, W","center":[16.372605,48.208728]}. On 401 or 403 see Access and limits. Each feature has place_name, center (lon,lat) and geometry. types=address limits the results to addresses; without it a street or place can come first even for a house number.

data:
Annotation. Extra values per route segment, for example speed or elevation. Requested with annotations.
Contours. Lines of equal elevation. Tileset contours.
DEM. Digital elevation model, here stored as Terrain-RGB tiles. See Terrain-RGB.
DSM / DTM. Digital surface model (including buildings and trees) and digital terrain model (bare ground).
Geocoding. Turning an address or place name into coordinates. Reverse geocoding does the opposite.
Glyphs. Font data that MapLibre loads to draw labels. See Styles API.
Isochrone. An area reachable from a point within a given time or distance.
Orthophoto. Rectified aerial photograph.
PMTiles. Single-file archive of tiles, read with HTTP range requests. The mapx styles read their tiles from PMTiles; the page must register the pmtiles:// protocol for that (maplibregl.addProtocol, see First map). Otherwise your own applications use TileJSON or {z}/{x}/{y}.
Profile. The kind of traveler for routing: driving, driving-traffic, driving-truck, cycling, cycling-mtb, walking.
Sprite. Image atlas with the icons of a style.
Style. A JSON document that tells the map which data to draw and how. mapx offers streets, satellite, outdoors and more; all styles are listed in the style reference.
Tile. A square piece of map addressed as {z}/{x}/{y}. See Tile scheme.
TileJSON. A small JSON description of a tileset: URL template, zoom range, bounds, attribution.
Tileset. A named collection of tiles, for example streets or contours. See Tilesets.

data:
mapx is a set of maps and location APIs for Austria. All data comes from official open sources (BEV, GIP.at, ASFINAG, GeoSphere Austria, ÖBB, Copernicus Sentinel-2 and others; full list under Sources and licenses). A free account and API token are required (Access and limits).
Product What you get Start Maps Vector and raster tiles, ready-made styles (streets with the time-of-day variants streets-dawn, streets-dusk, streets-night, satellite, satellite-current (Sentinel-2, current satellite image), satellite-streets, outdoors, outdoors-winter, light, dark, traffic-day, traffic-night, the relief maps relief, relief-contours, relief-light, relief-dark, plus 3D variants such as outdoors-3d, satellite-3d and streets-3d; list under Styles), TileJSON Maps Search Geocoding, type-ahead Search Box, address autofill and validation Search Navigation Routes for car, truck, bike and foot, isochrones, matrices, map matching, tolls Navigation Traffic Incident reports, motorway speed limits, a traffic layer Traffic Transit Public transport journeys, stops, departures Transit Static images PNG or WebP maps with pins, paths and GeoJSON Static images Elevation and terrain Heights, elevation profiles, terrain and surface models Elevation Weather and environment Measurements, forecast, warnings, radar and weather tiles, air quality, climate Weather The APIs follow the conventions of well-known web mapping services: the same URL shapes, GeoJSON responses and MapLibre-compatible styles. Existing MapLibre, Leaflet or OpenLayers code needs few changes.

Each tileset is available as TileJSON and XYZ tiles through the Tiles API and is part of the styles. The data is licensed CC BY 4.0 (exception: Sentinel-2), see Attribution and license.
Tileset Type Zoom As of streets vector z0–16 2026-04-01 contours vector z10–16 2025-09-15 terrain-rgb DEM z5–16 2025-09-15 dsm DEM z5–16 2025-09-15 orthophoto raster z5–18 2025-10-03 orthophoto-flight-blocks vector z6–17 2025-10-03 rest-areas vector z7–14 2026-11-20 sharing vector z8–14 2026-11-20 bike-routes vector z5–14 2026-07-08 gip-poi vector z12–15 2026-07-08 sentinel2 raster z5–z13 daily sentinel2-date raster z5–z13 daily sentinel2-ndvi raster z5–z13 daily sentinel2-ndwi raster z5–z13 daily sentinel2-ndsi raster z5–z13 daily The Sentinel-2 tilesets (Sentinel-2 current and four derived products) are replaced daily instead of versioned, so they show “daily” instead of a reference date.
Use a tileset by name:
map.addSource("contours", { type: "vector", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/contours.json" }); All requests to tiles.mapx.at need a token, see Access and limits. MapLibre sources send it via transformRequest, tile URLs take ?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN.
The TileJSON address is https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/{tileset}.json.

Cycle routes and mountain bike trails from the open data set of the Austrian road graph platform (GIP.at, GIPOGD), EuroVelo routes included. In the style streets they form the layer group bike_routes (off by default); see Tourism.

Use cases

Geometry: LineZoom: z10–16Layer: contour_l
Elevation contours in four levels of detail.
Field Type Description ele number Elevation of the line in metres above sea level. index number 1 for index contours (major lines), otherwise 0. Possible values Meaning 0 Regular contour 1 Index contour (major line, usually labelled) lvl number Detail level of the contour; equals the map zoom level from which it is shown (interval 100 m, 50 m, 20 m, 10 m). data:
The DSM is the counterpart to the DTM: it shows the surface including buildings, trees and bridges. Encoding, tile size and zoom levels are identical; all clients and formulas of the DTM apply unchanged.
Use cases
Building and vegetation heightnDSM as DSM minus DTM in the client Solar planningRoof and shading heights as a basis Visibility and shadingSurface including buildings and forest 3D city and landscape viewsSurface as terrain in the browser Elevation profilesProfile over the surface

Send the token with every request: add the transformRequest from First map to the map options.

data.notes#Notes: Quantization 0.1 m. The finest level is z16 (about 0.8 m per pixel at 48° N); beyond that the client scales up. Accuracy corresponds to the official BEV source. Buildings and vegetation reflect the time of the survey flight, not the reference date. Outside the data the value is a smooth continuation, not a measurement (as with the DTM). Building and vegetation height (nDSM = DSM − DTM) can be computed in the client from both tile sets.
data.source-and-currency#Source and currency:
The DSM is derived from the BEV ALS-DOM 1 m (airborne laser scanning, surface). The reference date is in the specifications and the file name; a file never changes, a new release is a new file.
Source: BEV ALS-DOM 1 m, reference date 15 Sep 2025. Same encoding as the DTM: Mapbox Terrain-RGB with 0.1 m quantization, 512 px, lossless WebP.

data:
A satellite image of Austria that updates every day: each pixel shows a robust value from the most recent cloud- and shadow-free Sentinel-2 acquisitions (rolling best-pixel composite). Resolution 10 m, Web Mercator, WebP, 512 px, z5 to z13 (the client overzooms beyond that). The acquisition date of every pixel is kept in the underlying store.
Use cases
Current backgroundSatellite view that is not years old Seeing changeSnow cover, harvest, windthrow, construction sites on a 10 m grid Overview and planningLandscape, vegetation and water at a glance
data.add-to-your-map#Add to your map:
MapLibreLeafletcurl const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, container: "map", center: [15.334, 48.227], zoom: 11, style: { version: 8, sources: { s2: { type: "raster", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/sentinel2.json", tileSize: 512 } }, layers: [{ id: "s2", type: "raster", source: "s2" }] } }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once("load", () => map.getContainer().querySelector(".maplibregl-compact-show")?.classList.remove("maplibregl-compact-show")); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) TileJSON provides zoom range, bounds and attribution. Send the token with every request: add the transformRequest from First map to the map options. The ready-made style satellite-current (Sentinel-2 with roads and labels) is available at /v1/styles/satellite-current; it is not available as a static map image or static tile.
L.tileLayer("https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/sentinel2/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN", { tileSize: 512, zoomOffset: -1, minZoom: 5, maxNativeZoom: 13, maxZoom: 18, crossOrigin: true, attribution: "mapx.at; Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026" }).addTo(map); curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/sentinel2.json curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -o tile.webp https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/sentinel2/13/4444/2839.webp The tileset is replaced daily (fixed tileset sentinel2, no versioned file name). The TileJSON states the date in the field mapx:reference_date (most recent ingested scene). Cached for 5 minutes.

Required under the Copernicus terms of use (free, full and open) for modified data:
mapx.at; Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026 The year is the year of acquisition; MapLibre picks up the text from TileJSON or PMTiles. More: License.
data.index-and-date-overlays#Index and date o:
Four further fixed tilesets are derived from the same composite. They are transparent where there is no value, so they work as overlays on sentinel2, a satellite image or a street map. All are WebP, 512 px, z5 to z13, same attribution; each is replaced daily together with sentinel2. They appear in /v1/tiles only once the file exists. The TileJSON carries the value range and colour ramp in mapx:legend.
Tileset Shows Value and colour sentinel2-date Acquisition date per pixel age in days before mapx:reference_date: 0 green, 20 yellow, 45 orange, 90 red, 180 dark red sentinel2-ndvi Vegetation, (NIR - red) / (NIR + red) -0.1 grey, 0.05 bare, 0.2 sand, 0.4 light green, 0.85 dark green sentinel2-ndwi Water, (green - NIR) / (green + NIR) only values above 0: light blue (0) to dark blue (0.7) sentinel2-ndsi Snow, (green - SWIR) / (green + SWIR) only values from 0.4: light blue to white (0.8); water is excluded by a NIR threshold map.addSource("ndvi", { type: "raster", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/sentinel2-ndvi.json", tileSize: 512 }); map.addLayer({ id: "ndvi", type: "raster", source: "ndvi", paint: { "raster-opacity": 0.8 } }); In the mapx viewer they are the overlays “Acquisition date”, “Vegetation (NDVI)”, “Water (NDWI)” and “Snow (NDSI)” in the layer group Satellite, with legend and opacity slider.
data.notes#Notes: The image mixes several days (the date is stored per pixel); dense ground fog lasting weeks can remain despite the filter. 10 m source resolution: z13 is the last level with real gain in detail.
data.source-and-method#Source and method: Source: Sentinel-2 L2A (surface reflectance) from ESA/Copernicus as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF via Element84 Earth Search (STAC, AWS Open Data). Only bands B04, B03, B02 (10 m) and the scene classification SCL (20 m) are read, with HTTP range requests. Mask: SCL classes 4 (vegetation), 5 (bare soil), 6 (water) and 11 (snow) are valid; clouds, shadows, cirrus, dark and unclassified pixels do not count. The mask is eroded by 40 m, and pixels with a very high blue share (haze) are dropped, except snow. Robust value instead of latest value: each pixel keeps its last 5 valid observations. The output is a value of medium brightness among the observations of the 45 days before the most recent one; outliers (too blue, too bright, too dark) against the median are discarded. The image stays current while haze and thin clouds drop out. Gaps: older observations fill pixels that were never clear recently; remaining holes are filled from neighbouring pixels. Seams: each scene is brightness-matched to the stored data, and edges between acquisition days are blended softly.
data.tilejson-zoom-and-update#TileJSON, zoom: TileJSON https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/sentinel2.json Tiles https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/sentinel2/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp Zoom z5 to z13 (6.4 m per pixel at z13 on 47.5 degrees north; the source is 10 m) Format WebP, 512 px, Web Mercator Coverage Austria (tiles at the border extend abroad) Update daily at 02:00; new scenes are merged into the store, then the file is replaced atomically

The DTM is an elevation tile set for all of Austria: ground height without buildings and vegetation, encoded as color (Terrain-RGB). It works directly as raster-dem for hillshading and 3D terrain in MapLibre, Mapbox GL and compatible clients.
Use cases

MapLibreQGISPythoncurl const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, container: "map", center: [12.694, 47.074], zoom: 11, pitch: 60, style: { version: 8, sources: { dem: { type: "raster-dem", url: "https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb.json", tileSize: 512, encoding: "mapbox" } }, terrain: { source: "dem", exaggeration: 1.2 }, layers: [{ id: "hill", type: "hillshade", source: "dem" }] } }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once("load", () => map.getContainer().querySelector(".maplibregl-compact-show")?.classList.remove("maplibregl-compact-show")); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) map.on("click", (e) => console.log(map.queryTerrainElevation(e.lngLat))); Send the token with every request: add the transformRequest from First map to the map options.
In the Browser panel, right-click XYZ Tiles, New Connection. URL https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp?access_token=YOUR_TOKEN, Min. Zoom 5, Max. Zoom 16, tile resolution 512. The layer shows the raw tiles (encoded color). Elevations follow from the formula in “Encoding” ((R*65536 + G*256 + B)*0.1 - 10000), for example in the Raster Calculator on the three bands. # pip install pillow numpy requests import io import numpy as np import requests from PIL import Image z, x, y = 12, 2192, 1439 # Grossglockner r = requests.get(f"https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb/{z}/{x}/{y}.webp", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"}, timeout=30) r.raise_for_status() tile = r.content rgb = np.asarray(Image.open(io.BytesIO(tile)).convert("RGB")).astype(np.uint32) hoehe = -10000 + (rgb[..., 0] * 65536 + rgb[..., 1] * 256 + rgb[..., 2]) * 0.1 print(hoehe.shape, hoehe.min(), hoehe.max()) # one tile via the XYZ endpoint curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -o kachel.webp https://tiles.mapx.at/v1/tiles/terrain-rgb/12/2192/1439.webp

Required under CC BY 4.0. Text:

data.encoding#Encoding: height_m = -10000 + (R · 65536 + G · 256 + B) · 0.1 Theoretical value range −10000 m to +1,667,721.5 m in steps of 0.1 m; in Austria the values lie between about 115 m (Lake Neusiedl) and about 3,798 m (Grossglockner). Values are rounded to 0.1 m when written (round half to even at exactly .5, see Rust code above); values outside the range are clamped. WebP lossless: lossy compression would directly corrupt the encoded elevations. Do not use alpha information; read the RGB bands unchanged (no color management, no premultiplied alpha). 512 × 512 pixels, no border (no 1 px skirt). In MapLibre specify tileSize: 512 and encoding: "mapbox". In detail: Terrain-RGB.
data.horizontal-resolution-by-zoom#Horizontal:
At 47.5° N, 512 px tiles, Web Mercator:
Zoom m per pixel Tile edge (km) Note z5 1,652 846 z6 826 423 z7 413 212 z8 207 106 z9 103 53 z10 52 26 z11 26 13 z12 13 6.61 z13 6.46 3.30 z14 3.23 1.65 z15 1.61 0.83 z16 0.81 0.41 highest stored level (≈ 1 m source) z17 0.40 0.21 overzoom (client) The data come from a 1 m raster. z16 (about 0.8 m per pixel) is the finest level and preserves the resolution of the source. There are no tiles above z16: from z17 MapLibre scales up the z16 tile (set maxzoom: 16).
data.live-map#Live map: BEV – ALS-DTM 1 m (Stichtag 15.09.2025), CC BY 4.0"> 3D terrain Hillshade Click the map: elevation and tile RGB. This map requires JavaScript. Clicking reads the tile of the current zoom level (z16 at most) via range request, decodes the pixel at the click point with the formula under “Encoding” and shows elevation and RGB value. With 3D enabled, the value of queryTerrainElevation is shown as well.
data.notes#Notes: Quantization 0.1 m. The deviation from the source is within the rounding range (at most 0.05 m). Vertical accuracy per BEV ± 0.50 m, see Vertical resolution and accuracy. The DTM shows the terrain without buildings, trees and bridges. For the surface there is the DSM. Coverage is the rectangle 9.53–17.17° E, 46.37–49.02° N. Outside Austria and in gaps the value is a smooth continuation of the terrain, not a measurement.
data.source-and-currency#Source and currency:
The DTM is derived from the BEV ALS-DTM 1 m (airborne laser scanning, terrain only). The reference date is in the specifications and the file name; a file never changes, a new release is a new file.
Source: BEV (Austrian Federal Office of Metrology and Surveying), reference date 15 Sep 2025.
data.specifications#Specifications: Tilesetterrain-rgb Reference date 2025-09-15 Format webp, encoding mapbox, 512 px Zoom levels z5–z16 Bounds (WGS84) 9.5306 / 46.3697 / 17.1661 / 49.0235 (W/S/O/N) Vertical resolution 0.1 m (Terrain-RGB) Vertical accuracy (source) ± 0.50 m per BEV, larger in high mountains Height reference EVRF2000 Austria, orthometric (EPSG:9274) License CC BY 4.0
data.vertical-resolution-and-accuracy#Vertica:
Value Meaning Vertical resolution 0.1 m smallest height step of the encoding Deviation from source ≤ 0.05 m rounding during encoding, otherwise unchanged (lossless) Vertical accuracy of the source ± 0.50 m stated by BEV for the ALS-DTM; larger deviations are possible in high mountains Height reference EVRF2000 Austria orthometric heights (EPSG:9274), as in the source The encoding is five times finer than the accuracy of the survey, so it does not limit quality.
In the overview levels z15 to z5 each pixel is the mean of the finer level. The vertical resolution stays 0.1 m, but small peaks and summits are smoothed. For exact point heights read z16 or use the elevation API.

All requests need a token (Access and limits); in server code use a secret token (mx_sk_…) and never ship it in a web page.
Fleet and delivery software needs a route that a truck can really drive, travel times for many pairs, a good order of stops and the current traffic reports. All four are one request each. Coordinates are lon,lat, times are seconds, distances metres.

data.plan-the-tour#Plan the tour:
POST /v1/optimization assigns jobs to vehicles and orders them: capacity, time windows, service times (seconds), start and end per vehicle. At most 10 vehicles, 50 jobs and 60 distinct locations per request. Secret token (mx_sk_…) from a server only; a public token gets 403 pk-not-allowed.
const body = { profile: "driving", vehicles: [{ id: 1, start: [16.3725, 48.2083], end: [16.3725, 48.2083], time_window: [28800, 61200] }], services: [ { id: 1, location: [15.6256, 48.2049], service: 300, time_windows: [[32400, 43200]] }, { id: 2, location: [14.2858, 48.3069], service: 600 }, ], }; const res = await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/optimization", { method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json", Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" }, body: JSON.stringify(body) }); const tour = await res.json(); console.log(tour.routes[0].steps.map((s) => s.id ?? s.type), tour.unassigned); // unassigned: jobs that did not fit Draw the result with one directions request through tour.routes[0].steps locations (up to 25 points); see the tour planning example.
data.traffic#Traffic:
driving-traffic uses the reports of ASFINAG and EVIS.AT: binding closures are avoided, non-binding closures are avoided where possible, and on motorways the speed limits currently shown on variable message signs slow down the travel time. There is no area-wide measured traffic flow (speeds on every road, congestion as “flow”); reported jams without a closure do not change the route, they only show up as incidents. Incidents on the route come with incidents=true in legs[].incidents. For a region, list the active incidents or show the traffic style:
const bbox = [14.5, 47.8, 16.9, 48.6]; // Lower Austria const { features } = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/traffic/incidents?bbox=${bbox}&active=true&type=construction&limit=50`, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); console.log(features.length, features[0]?.properties.road, features[0]?.properties.text); The map style traffic-day shows the current reports and closures and, on motorways, the sections with a speed limit from variable message signs (no area-wide traffic flow); see the example. Traffic data: ASFINAG / EVIS.AT (CC BY 4.0).
data.travel-times-for-many-pairs#Travel times:
matrix answers all pairs in one request, up to the limits of the Matrix API. Use sources and destinations (indices) to ask for one row only.
const depots = [[16.3725, 48.2085], [15.3294, 48.2272], [14.2858, 48.3069]]; const q = depots.map((p) => p.join(",")).join(";"); const m = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/matrix/driving/${q}?annotations=duration,distance`, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); console.log(m.durations[0][1] / 60, "min", m.distances[0][1] / 1000, "km"); // Vienna to Melk
data.truck-routes#Truck routes:
The profile driving-truck takes the vehicle size and avoids roads with matching weight, height, width and length limits and bans. Without parameters it assumes 40 t, 4 m high and 2.55 m wide.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving-truck/15.6256,48.2049;15.3294,48.2272?weight=40&height=4&width=2.55&length=16.5&truck_type=semi&overview=false" \ | jq '.routes[0] | {distance, duration, truck, toll_go_km: .toll.truck_go_km}' routes[0].toll.truck_go_km is the length subject to the GO toll; per step it is truck_go_m. Speeds follow truck limits (80 km/h on motorways). District-wide bans from free-text ordinances are not routed: affected roads come as steps[].notices[] with type: "truck_restriction"; show them to the dispatcher. For cars, exclude=toll and exclude=motorway avoid toll sections and motorways (profiles driving, driving-traffic and driving-truck); exclude=ferry works for every profile except driving-traffic.
In JavaScript:
const q = new URLSearchParams({ weight: 40, height: 4, width: 2.55, length: 16.5, truck_type: "semi", steps: true }); const r = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/driving-truck/15.6256,48.2049;15.3294,48.2272?${q}`, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); const notices = r.routes[0].legs.flatMap((l) => l.steps).flatMap((s) => s.notices ?? []);

data: Municipal tools work with addresses and need to be understood by residents, and the data is free to use under CC BY 4.0. mapx is free with an API token (Access and limits); replace YOUR_TOKEN with your own. The pieces below combine the address register, the timetable and the map for the web page of a municipality.
data.check-addresses#Check addresses:
Forms for registrations, applications and reports should accept only existing addresses. address/validate compares the input with the address register and returns match, corrected, ambiguous or not_found with the corrected address and coordinates.
const q = new URLSearchParams({ street: "Haubtplatz", housenumber: "1", postcode: "3390", place: "Melk" }); const r = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/address/validate?${q}`, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); console.log(r.status, r.deviations.map((d) => `${d.field}: ${d.input} > ${d.expected}`), r.address?.full_address ?? r.candidates?.map((c) => c.full_address)); While the person types, offer address autofill; for lists with many addresses use POST /v1/geocode/batch (Search), secret token (mx_sk_…) from a server only, otherwise 403 pk-not-allowed.
data.departures-at-the-town-hall#Departures a:
Residents ask “When does the next bus go?”. The scheduled timetable is one request away:
const H = { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } }; const { stops: [stop] } = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/stops?near=15.3294,48.2272&radius=400&limit=1", H)).json(); const { departures } = await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/departures?stop=${encodeURIComponent(stop.id)}&limit=6`, H)).json(); document.querySelector("#abfahrten").replaceChildren(...departures.map((d) => Object.assign(document.createElement("li"), { textContent: `${d.time.slice(11, 16)} ${d.line.name} → ${d.headsign}` }))); On a map, the example does the same with a click. See Transit departures. Timetable data: ÖBB-Personenverkehr AG, data source Mobilitätsverbünde Österreich (CC BY 4.0).

data:
All requests need a token; replace YOUR_TOKEN with your own (Access and limits).
Visitors ask “Which way by bike, how steep is it, and what is the weather?”. The answers come from the same API: routes with the profiles cycling and cycling-mtb, a profile of the heights, the signposted cycle routes on the map and the forecast for the destination.
data.elevation-profile#Elevation profile:
Every tour page benefits from a profile. Feed the route geometry (2 to 512 points; the default simplified route geometry fits) into the elevation API:
const route = (await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/cycling/15.3294,48.2272;15.6141,48.4097", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json()).routes[0]; // the default overview=simplified keeps the line below the 512-point limit const line = route.geometry.coordinates.map((c) => c.join(",")).join(";"); const p = (await (await fetch(`https://api.mapx.at/v1/elevation/profile?coordinates=${line}&samples=120`, { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json()).properties; console.log(`up ${Math.round(p.ascent_m)} m, down ${Math.round(p.descent_m)} m, ${Math.round(p.min_m)}-${Math.round(p.max_m)} m`); // p.distances[i] (m from start) and p.elevations[i] (m) give the chart The height model is the official DTM of the BEV. See Elevation profile for a finished chart and the live example.

data.reachability-for-the-area#Reachability f:
Which destinations can guests reach in 30 minutes by bike? One isochrone request:
const iso = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/isochrone/cycling/15.3294,48.2272?contours_minutes=15,30,45", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); // largest area first map.addSource("reach", { type: "geojson", data: iso }); map.addLayer({ id: "reach", type: "fill", source: "reach", paint: { "fill-color": "#2346d8", "fill-opacity": 0.12 } }); For public transport to the trailhead use the profile bike_transit (GET /v1/directions/bike_transit/{start};{end}, Transit) to ride to the stop.
data.routes-for-bikes#Routes for bikes:
cycling prefers cycle paths and signposted routes and rates unpaved sections and steep grades worse. cycling-mtb prefers forest tracks and singletrails. With steps=true every step carries the type of infrastructure and the surface, routes[].summary has ascent, descent and maximum grade.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/cycling-mtb/15.3294,48.2272;15.4,48.3?steps=true&overview=false" \ | jq '.routes[0] | {distance, duration, summary}' const r = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/directions/cycling/15.3294,48.2272;15.6141,48.4097?steps=true&alternatives=true&annotations=elevation", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); console.log(r.routes.map((x) => `${(x.distance / 1000).toFixed(1)} km, up ${x.summary?.ascent_m} m`));
data.show-the-cycle-routes#Show the cycle rou:
The streets style contains the signposted cycle and MTB routes as the layer group bike_routes. Switch it on with the style metadata, or let the user toggle it:
const TOKEN = "YOUR_TOKEN"; // the style uses PMTiles sources: load pmtiles.js as in the examples maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", new pmtiles.Protocol().tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ attributionControl: false, container: "map", style: "https://api.mapx.at/v1/styles/streets", center: [15.45, 48.3], zoom: 10, transformRequest: (url) => ({ url: /^https:\/\/([\w-]+\.)?mapx\.at\//.test(url) && !url.includes("access_token=") ? url + (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + "access_token=" + TOKEN : url }), }); map.addControl(new maplibregl.AttributionControl({ compact: true })); map.once("load", () => map.getContainer().querySelector(".maplibregl-compact-show")?.classList.remove("maplibregl-compact-show")); // start collapsed (MapLibre keeps it open until the first drag) map.on("load", () => { // switch on the layers of the group bike_routes (off by default in the style) for (const id of map.getStyle().metadata["mapx:groups"].bike_routes) map.setLayoutProperty(id, "visibility", "visible"); }); The example Route calculates and draws a route on the map (MapLibre, OpenLayers, Leaflet).
data.weather-for-the-destination#Weather for: const f = await (await fetch("https://api.mapx.at/v1/weather/forecast?lon=12.694&lat=47.074&hours=12", { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" } })).json(); // Grossglockner console.log(f.hours.map((h) => `${new Date(h.time).toLocaleTimeString("en-GB", { hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit", timeZone: "Europe/Vienna" })} ${h.temperature_c}°C ${h.precipitation_mm} mm`).join("\n")); GET /v1/weather/current?lon=…&lat=… gives the measurements of the nearest stations. As a map layer see the weather overlay. Weather data: GeoSphere Austria (CC BY 4.0).
